I didn't like you pretty much had to restart to see how some missions were going to go down -- where the creeper went (18: The Tide) or how strong and numerous the drones were (Barbarian Hordes).
Overall though, it was a lot of fun, and cheap for the time. There are also lots of user-created maps, but I couldn't find a way to sort by ranking. Most are also very well-rated, so it might be hard to find the better ones in there.

Creeper World 2 changes from the first game with a foreward perspective instead of a top down. While the gameplay is similar to the first in the series, there are obvious differences, such as lack of a large spiderlike network and the ability to dig into the rock. Many new gimmicks are introduced into this game, notably the ability to destroy emitters, which carried over to the 3rd game. At first some of the concepts such as the shapes the creeper made were hard to understand, but with time it became clear.  Unfortunately, for me it feels like the gimmicks were not used to their full potential, though they were dug into during the bonus missions, and this could be solved with more bonus missions. Specifically, the units given to you during the final level are only available on the last missions of the story and bonus campaigns, and it would have been interesting for them to have seen more use.
In short CW2 is a great addition to the series, and although it has some differences from the other games in the series, any Knuckle Cracker fan should enjoy it for its gameplay and low price.

HIGHLY RECOMMENDED.  In my opinion, Creeper World 2 is better than CW3.  This is unexpected - prior to playing CW2, I had serious doubts about CW2's side-view perspective, as opposed to the top-down view of CW1, CW3 and PF.  However, the side-view, combined with the tactical balance between empty-space and filled space (dirt), provide more interesting tactical choices.  Gameplay is deeper and richer.  Your units and the creeper can occupy empty space.  Filled space (dirt) forms a barrier blocking both your units and the creeper.  However, you can choose to remove most of the dirt.  Most of the tactical challenge comes from deciding which dirt to remove, and when, and then building your economy in the space you create by removing dirt.  I would rank all four Knucklecracker games as follows:  CW2 > CW3 > PF > CW1.

The original release for this game was to be December 4, 2013. A bit late, eh?
Sure, Chucklefish may not have been able to deliver on time, but look at Valve's record. They weren't bashed for being late because of Valve Time.  The game is getting much better, and is almost to it's official release (2 updates until) and is really good compared to what it may have been if it released when planned.

This game has done exactly what it aimed to do in the first place: let people explore.
Although, it is still in beta, with many additions, bosses, quests and mechanics yet to be created in the universe. (with whips being planned in the next update, upon writing this.)
However, this game is not flawless; the AI is quite stupid, with pathfinding that matches an acrobat missing their inner ear, and the game making some parts of itself feel unneccessary, and the framrate dying at certain buildings made by the devs (which is being fixed).
Conclusion: You should try it, sometime, at the least.

Creeper World 3 seems to have tons of reviews and lots of popularity, but the first two feel neglected. Of the three Creeper World 3 is obviously a masterpiece, and has the most interesting story, but the first two are still well-made and offer a lot of background information, and this one in particular has a different (side-view) perspective, which makes it interesting, because downward gravity often plays a role.
For those who haven't played any game in this series, it's a tower defense game where you can move the towers around and are fighting a single enemy (a giant slime) which is emitted from certain points. Your goal is to destroy enough of the slime to reach those points and destroy those slime-generation points. Often it feels as if you too are "creeping" your towers forward.
What makes these games so enjoyable to me though isn't just the interesting gameplay (though that's very well done) but also the story. As the developer of "Immortal Defense" I know a few things about tower defense games with stories, and I'd say that this series (especially the third one) are almost certainly worth trying out if you enjoyed my game.
The only negative about these games is that they are available for free elsewhere -- there are some small updates to the Steam versions, like a new soundtrack, but it's for you to decide if those changes worth 5 dollars when you can play it for free on other sites like Kongregate. At the very least, it means you can play the free online version first to decide if you like it. Another slight negative is that in the first two games (including this one, Creeper World 2) the GUI / user-interface feels extremely rushed, and is often poorly designed. But I didn't let that get in the way of enjoying the game.

I expected a mediocre game. Terraria - which is already just "minecraft but 2d" - in space. So in other words, I expected 2D minecraft in space.
Yeah. It's 2D Minecraft in space. But holy crap it is so much MORE. It has all the features you'd expect from a 3rd generation minecraft clone, but combined with all sorts of other features. It has a lot of RPG elements, and I do love RPGs. Quests, for instance. And there's actual lore - not a ton, mind you, but everything makes sense and it forms a cohesive game. The graphics are beautiful, too, and so is the soundtrack. I haven't had it very long, and yes - it's POSSIBLE that the charm will wear off soon. But I haven't even scratched the surface of the game, really. I haven't played multiplayer at all yet, which will doubtless be even better. And I hear - though I may have heard wrong - that it's easy to mod Starbound, too.
If you want a simple list of its selling points, here's what did it for me:
*Sandbox combined with RPG elements in an extremely elegant and well-thought-out manner
*Fanastic character customization which really adds to the immersion and individuality
*It's fun enough even when I'm not playing with friends
*Cute, charming graphics
*Pretty music
*Playable even on my horribly slow laptop!

Honestly this game is one of the biggest suprises that I had this year. I bought this game expecting a clone from GTA or Saints Row, but I come out with a game that has a completely unique feel to it in every way. Not everything about Sleeping Dogs is perfect, but by no means is anything broken.
In terms of gameplay and setting you are in modern day Hong Kong as an undercover cop with some serious baggage who is trying to take down the local Triads. You can go almost everywhere on the map. Some areas are locked out for a time but through some missions you can eventually reach these places.
Most of what you will be doing in the game is completing missions from either the Triads or taking cases from the police, with some favors or sidemissions thrown in between. One thing I have to admit about Sleeping Dogs is that it isn't much of a sandbox. Consider it more of a jungle gym. There are somethings to do outside of it, but you will mainly be playing inside of the bars. Much like Mafia 2 if a comparison is needed.
Combat is a very central role in Sleeping Dogs and mostly takes place in fist fighting. If you have ever played Batman Arkhakm Asylum then you will be just fine in the combat in this game. Striking and countering with some ground game and throws are in; and can be really graphic at times. The other side of combat is shooting. It is  a very typical third person shooter affair; hide behind cover here, pop out there, headshot here, slow motion there. Nothing too special, however, it is solid though it does not occur often compared to the fist fights.
Driving is also a big part of Sleeping Dogs just like most open world games. There a plenty of cars to steal, but you can also buy many cars as well and store them in multiple garages. I mainly did this because I would need certain types of cars for how I would feel. Apparently once you buy the cars you also buy every right to every car model like it as you can destroy your car completely; call your valet and he will bring the same exact car in prestine condition for free! Controls are fine nothing ridiculous or hard to learn.
The main thing that kept me playing however is the story. It just grabs you from the beginning and honestly makes you think. How far are you willing to go in order to do something right? Questioning loyalty, greed, murder. It's all there and it's all compelling.
If you want an open world game with a great story and good gameplay Sleeping Dogs is for you!

What do you get when you mix claymation, musical writing, and simple point-and-click mechanics together with a surreal-seeming aesthetic and slightly wonky humour?
Well, if you knew, I'd like you to tell me. However, what we have on hand here is Dominique Pimp-...Pampel-...Pumpernick..Whatever. A Flash game created by an independant games designer with an ear for catchy tunes and memorable lyrics.
This game is presented in the style of clayfighters 64, or The Neverhood, with a heavily Noire-ish turn and grayscale colouration. The character figurines are rough, simple and yet manage to be recognisable and easily identifyable. This is helped in no small part by the voice acting, with varied voices provided for all the characters. While certain characters' voices might fall apart in some musical segments, on the whole, the song fragments are well-written and do a fine job of explaining the situation or the topic presented.
The story follows Dominique, the PI of indeterminate gender with an effeminate voice on his/her mission to find a missing pop star. The story does play into some twists and turns, and while some of them are obvious, or heavily foreshadowed, none of them are jarring with the story. The game is heavily linear, though, with only a single solution present to each puzzle until the ultimate choice at the end. So unless you wish to trawl for trading cards, there's very little reason to replay the game.
if you like musicals, or games with a certain sense of silliness about them, then this game may be for you, if you can forgive the fact it's coded in flash. (encoded rather loudly, I might add) For veteran point-and-click gamers, though, it will ultimately prove to be a relatively shallow entry into the genre, carried somewhat by a fun and catchy musical score.
My positive reccomendation, then, does have some caveats to it. If you play an instrument, splurge on the sheet music for a few short pieces to play.

At its core, this game is grind, grind, grind. I, for one, have an addictive personality, so I don't really care about that. There is literally no other point to this game than grinding.
When you first open the "game," you are presented with an ugly-as-heck login screen. Maybe consists of 90 pixels. And the game is not automatically in full screen. Seems like a bad sign. You will input your info and pick World 2 because that is where all the cool kids go. Once logged in, you will be sent to tutorial island. Yeah. ˙puɐlsI lɐıɹoʇn⊥. You will midly suffer there for about 10 minutes while you try to walk through gates that cannot and will not open until you finish everything every guy has to say to you even though you have 1,000 hours experience of Runescape. I mean, what?
After that mess, you'll take a magic boat to a country called Dorpat where real people, low or high level gather for seemingly no reason at all. You will have no idea where to go. No f*cking idea. No quest helper, nothing. If you have patience, you will walk around for a while until you either find the chest with all your stuff in it, or start fighting a chicken without a knife. Eventually you will find your quests. You will start your quests. You will get another quest and realise that you don't know where it is. You have to find it on your own. Eventually, you will get to the point where you have to go OUT of Dorpat and find someplace else. The map won't seem very helpful, but after you open it, there's ANOTHER secret map in the left corner that gives a detailed depiction of the Hellhole you are about to endure for the next however many hours.
You will probably feel like everyone in this game is rich except you. In the chat, people usually talk about their hundreds of millions of dollars and you are sitting there with maybe 4,000 bux. No worries, you will advance quickly with all the Double XP going around. Even though everyone is rich, they are not a*sholes and are usually ALL nice. Except the mods. F*ck  the mods. Spam your Twitch livestream 3 times? Banned. Make a anti-joke? Banned. Refuse to pretend that there aren't bugs and glitches everywhere? Banned, banned, banned. You really don't get a second chance.
Maybe the devs have given up on the game, but the game is not dead at all. And hey, when the game says no level caps, it really means NO level caps, so go crazy.
Overall, free fun.
Pro tip: Don't trash the f*cking feathers. They seem like such a feeble item that drops off a level 1 Chicken/Hen, but if you really want to advance, market sell the s*it out of these.

You can get hooked to pirates pretty easily, Blackwake is no exception. If you enjoy doing tasks that reward you with score or titles then this is a game for you. There is no overarching reward and all it is is ship combat with fully modular ships that can break. From a technology standpoint this is a really amazing game concept. The game is currently the same two game types hosted on servers in Europe, you are either a brit or a pirate and you get to kill each other with cannons or different weapons.
You can expect the following in a session:
You join and chose your team, from there your entire team has to load the cannons and then you shoot each other if you play team deathmatch to reduce the amount of "Tickets" (Lives) the enemy has or by capturing the booty. You will be reloading cannons and yell at your captain to aim the ship correctly and you will fire your cannon hoping your captain did the ship angling right. You do this until all of the enemy tickets are gone.
In the other game type it is the game gameplay but once you are boarded your respawn time gets restricted and if no one is alive the other team wins.
Pros:
Modular Ship Destruction
Amazing Graphics
Cons:
Gameplay is repetative
No overarching goals for gameplay
Repetative
Unresponsive First Person weaponary
tl;dr If you like being a pirate then by all means jump at it!

I don't feel like reviewing Starbound is worth my time, so instead, I'll tell you the story of a tiger; a glorious tiger named "StoundBar".
As a cub, Stoundbar's bright colorful fur astounded everyone, and shined bright against all the other tigers around her. Tigers everywhere thought she would be the legend among them.
As she neared adolescence, her outstanding talent showed itself. Were there already fast tigers in the community? Sure, but Stound was faster. Were there tigers who were experts at hunting? Sure, but she brought in more game than anyone else. It became clear that she had potential.
And then it happened...
A circus came to her habitat and was swiping up other tigers, but when they saw Stoundbar, they stopped in their tracks. They released the other tigers and took her instead. Off to the circus. The circus... named "♥♥♥♥leChish"
At ♥♥♥♥leChish, her talent was displayed. Her best qualities; her running, her hunting skills, and others were all showcased for small audiences at first; introductory gigs where people got an exclusive glimpse of Stoundbar's excellence. Other acts, performances; other animals fell in her shadow. All people wanted to see was Stoundbar.
After awhile, ♥♥♥♥leChish began a fundraiser to develop Stoundbar's talents even further. Apparently, word of StoundBar's unique talent and glory had spread internationally, so their fundraiser raked in millions. By that time, they had their own place for their increasingly popular shows, but they decided that, with these new funds, a change of location was in order. Over almost the course of a year, they moved to a new location, and excitement for StoundBar waned the longer they took.
When they finally moved, however, ♥♥♥♥leChish Circus' popularity died, and with it, Stoundbar's did too.
And then came the abuse...
With Chucklefish--err, I mean.. ♥♥♥♥leChish seeking a desperate revival of Stoundbar's audience and notoriety, they began to beat and batter the last remnants of her brilliance out of her over time. They spent months at a time between shows pumping her with harmful steroids and hormones to try and boost her lore. Enhancements which seemed amazing on the surface were soon revealed to be harmful for her in reality. For about a month after Stoundbar, with her brand-new enhancements, were exposed to the world, her fans returned to the stadium. However, they got bored and stopped attending shows once again.
Eventually, ♥♥♥♥leChish fell into a depressing pattern; a downward spiral of desperate enhancements for Stoundbar which slowly began to kill her. The fans, however, rush back temperarily (in increasingly small numbers) and then retreat to other shows in only a matter of weeks.
Stoundbar's fur suddenly didn't seem so bright;
Her talents.. no longer special.
Starbound's era passed prematurely, and for that... all thanks can be given to the poor management of Chucklefish.
I was one of her fans; there from the first show she gave to the massive, cheering crowds.. and now all I can say is.. show's over kids, now it's time to move on to the next great act.

Titans should have been a free update, or at the very least a $5 DLC, not a full-priced game.  The new additions are nice.  Unfortunately, my previous difficulties with PA were not addressed: lack of supporting UI.  Simply put, PA is missing some critical components to UI that are required to make a game like this work (or honestly, any RTS).  I bought Titans hoping that they were.
What's wrong: There's NO MINIMAP.  Additionally, you're on a rotating globe with no visual identification as to where you are on that globe.  Where was your base?  Just pan around until you find it again.  Oh, the enemy is attacking on the other side of the planet?  Would be nice to know if that was a scout or a full-fledged invasion.  Important details :).  And that's just for a single planet.  Some maps have 6, and there's no UI information about which planets you even have troops on.  I love the idea of the game, and my friends and I gave it an honest shot with quite a few multiplayer games together.  Unfortunately, we all agreed that the UI just does not allow/support the gameplay, and the result is frustration.
Periodically I check the recent updates to see if there are any notes about improving the UI.  Nope.  I'll keep checking back, because I want to play this game, but they just don't come.  Frustrating death to such a great game concept for us.

"A delayed game is good eventually, a rushed game is bad forever" -Shigeru Miyamoto
The original release for this game was to be December 4, 2013. A bit late, eh?
Sure, Chucklefish may not have been able to deliver on time, but look at Valve's record. They weren't bashed for being late because of Valve Time.  The game is getting much better, and is almost to it's official release (2 updates until) and is really good compared to what it may have been if it released when planned.
So what I am saying is that putting this game off because of the heaps of negative reviews in the "Most Helpful" section isn't what this game deserves.
Now that I got that out of the way, let's make an actual review, shall we?
Overall: It's doing what it's set out to do.
When the beta first came out, it was so much different, monsters actually need to do attacks to damage you, the snow infantry armor was overpowered, and you could die of hunger, and freezing.
The Novakids didn't even exist in the game.
Today, that's all changed: Questing, ship upgrades, colonies, and really smooth generation of planets. This game managed to keep me interested in mining, which for some reason, Minecraft couldn't get me interested in that.
This game has done exactly what it aimed to do in the first place: let people explore.
Although, it is still in beta, with many additions, bosses, quests and mechanics yet to be created in the universe. (with whips being planned in the next update, upon writing this.)
However, this game is not flawless; the AI is quite stupid, with pathfinding that matches an acrobat missing their inner ear, and the game making some parts of itself feel unneccessary, and the framrate dying at certain buildings made by the devs (which is being fixed).
Conclusion: You should try it, sometime, at the least.

Stop motion animation, Adventure games, and musicals are three of my favorite things.
So, what happens when you throw them all in a blender? Magic, right? Well, kinda.
Dominique Pamplemousse in “It’s All Over Once The Fat Lady Sings!” is a combination of all those things. Using real clay characters, animated in the stop motion style, Pamplemousse tells the story of wealth inequality, gender politics, and detective work, while having the characters break out into song.
At times, this makes the game transcend all media I have seen, while you and your angry landlord have a singing fight while you run around the apartment looking for money, while at times, it hits the wrong note, sometimes quite literally.
The voices, including the singing ones are all done by one person, and all are "in character" when they sing, which unfortunately makes encounters with characters unbearable, as the teenager predictably has voice cracks, pops, and is generally off key quite a bit.
There's evidence in the game to support the theory that the unprofessional singing, and out of key songs is intentional, but it still is incredibly off putting when it rears it's head.
The art style is unique to say the least. This isn't the first time an adventure game, or any game for that matter has been stop motion animated, but each puppet is stylized as if it was made in pre-school, and the rest of the game tries to follow suit. Compared to the serious model quality of Aardmann (Wallace and Gromit) or Laika (Coraline), it's a refreshing take on the way stop motion models are made and animated, each character only having a few key frames of animation they run through.
The gameplay is less adventure game than I would have hoped. There are objects in the few environments that the game throws at you, that you can click on and interact with, and there are 2 light puzzles that shouldn't be too hard to get past. The rest of the game is carried out through dialogue boxes, where you interrogate people with the evidence you have found so far, occasionally causing a character or 2 to break out in song, singing about their feelings on a topic.
Dominique Pamplemousse is nominated for 4 IGF awards including the grand prize, and it's easy to see why: its fresh, clever, and thoughtful. However at times, it falls short of being astonishing, and ends up being mostly OK, with a few really great parts thrown in.
If you like strange, experimental games, you should probably give Pamplemousse a shot, its out there, clever, occasionally funny, and presents an interesting idea to the table: a musical video game. If it looks too strange for you, it probably is. It's quirky and weird, and that just may be it's downfall.

Love this game, almost much as I love what this game is striving to be. As a spiritual successor to Total Annihilation, this game gets much right, however similar to TA and Supreme Commander that followed, its ambitions far exceed its development budget and computational capacity for the time in which it was released. I can only hope similar to TA/SC, that future PC hardware will allow this game to be played at the scale it was envisaged. A poorly handled release and then re-release gave birth to many grumpy and vocal supporters, however the end product taken completely at face value is really a fantastic but flawed classic. If you are looking for your large scale RTS fix, and are tolerant of a few rough edges, then this should be great value. Do yourself a favour and look for PAMM (PA Mod Manager) and read up on many mods which help to smooth over a lot of User Interface and Gameplay quirks which the developers have never (and probably never will) had the opportunity to remedy. I backed this game heavily in the original Kickstarter, and whilst I often wonder how much much it could have turned out, I have no regrets at all.

Dominique Pamplemousse is a wonderfully written game about a non-bianary gendered dectective Dominique Pamplemousse who (while behind on their bills), gets hired by the owner of a record label to track down one of her missing stars, Casey Bingham.
This is a point and click game with a very lovely old-school claymation animation style, all done in black and white. When you ask characters questions, they explain in song as well, which I think is a really nice touch!
All in all, Dominique Pamplemousse is a really fun game, with great characters, and the fact that the main character is a non-binary gendered character really makes me happy (representation is important, yo!). All the characters that I've encountered are unique and well-fleshed out, and you learn facts about them all over the story, keeping the investigation alive, all while keeping you wondering how it all connects.
I highly reccomend this game if you want something different than your traditional point-and-click affairs, or if you want to see a non-binary character shine!

Although there are multiple endings (which seem to be determined only by the final choice), the game itself is pretty short. A single play-through takes about an hour. The game mechanics are simple but completely workable: you click on items on the screen to get dialogue or action options, or add things to your inventory. Most of the interactions are in the form of (frequently sung) dialogue, although there is some light puzzling, but it's mostly in the form of bouncing between locations as you open further dialogue options.
The story is cute and cleverly written. It's also pretty socially consious, but not annoyingly so. For the right audience, there are many clever bon mots and allusions peppered throughout the dialogue. The singing is horrible and off-key... but that's part of the charm. The story revolves around economic depression and autotuning in the music industry. It also playfully touches on gender identity in a way that makes me wish the game had been a bit longer and that had somehow been more of a story point.
The graphics... well, I think it's self-evident from the screenshots above. The models and animation are exceedingly simplistic, but they're charming in a Gumby kind-of way. I think the graphics work well in light of the humorous tone of the game, but your mileage may vary.
All in all I enjoyed the game, and hope this is not the last we see of Dominique Pamplemousse. If you like quirky, cleverly written off-beat games, give this one a shot, especially if it's on sale. But if you find out-of-key singing and simplisticly built and animated clay models to be grating, spend your money and time elsewhere.

My only complaint about Dominique Pamplemousse is that it's too short.
I enjoy the art and music styles for their handcrafted charm, but I really enjoy the what we learn - and infer - from playing through the game. I find the broad spectrum of real, normal, broken, annoying people to be refreshing - this is not a game that plays to the status quo of hetero-normative, masculine-centered culture that most gamers would like to imagine is real. Instead, we're thrust into the middle of a world where the protagonist just has better things to do than worry about gender identities and where every character has obvious fatal flaws.
Is this game for everyone? No, probably not. People who are incredibly judgmental and don't have the spark to enjoy unique creations from others should probably stick to mainstream titles. But for those who like to experience new and different things, this game is a brief look at the design skills of an up-and-coming Indie darling. The future looks very bright for Deirdra Kiai Productions.

Realm of the Mad God is an awesome game. There's nothing like it out there. It takes a standard MMO and boils it down to the most enjoyable parts - killing enemies and getting loot. It's simple and accessible, and as you approach endgame it adds more layers of complexity and difficulty while retaining the core game experience.
Despite having tons of content to experience, RotMG also suffers from many gamebreaking issues and the mistakes of its previous developer, Kabam. It's a Flash game. and a lot of content is hastily built on top of itself. It's prone to cheaters, game-changing hacked clients, and duping. It's just about destroyed the game economy, and the low-quality bandaids that Kabam implemented, like making more items soulbound or removing them, never attack the core problem.
Don't let that stop you, though - Kabam has been replaced with Deca Games, who, after just a couple of weeks, have proven themselves ready and willing to attack the real problem whenever they can. It's refreshing to have developers who communicate and are willing to see the game as we do, as gamers.
My hope is that Deca is willing to treat the game boldly. Kabam was never really willing to update the fundamental gameplay, besides the addition of useful pets and *two* new status effects (that's not very many). Potions and rare, untradeable items are fine as rewards, but, in my opinion, they're getting a bit stale. I could see updates like item enchantment, housing, guild updates, pet and other cosmetic upgrades really catching the attention of long-time players who're just kind of used to the way things are.
Overall, it's an amazing, game and you should definitely try it!

I am not a fan of visual novels (VN) – I mean, all the ones I have taken an interest in were eroge (VN focused on sex), principally when we are talking about girls’ love (GL) ones. Because of that, when I read about “Kindred Spirits on the Roof” (KSotR) being available on Steam, and about it being an 18+ VN, I was very hesitant and I was not sure if I should buy it or not. I thought it was only for the fan service, once all the screenshots I have seen of KSotR were 18+ scenes.
However, curiosity was stronger, so I decided on buying the game. First, because the plot seemed very interesting – with a bit of supernatural touch – and the most important factor: even being a VN, we do not have paths to follow or anything else: there are not lots of choices to make during the main route (MR) and anything we choose leads us to a common ending.
From the very beginning, the beautiful soundtrack captivated me, even the ambience sounds, and I the care LiarSoft had while developing this VN caught my attention: all the characters have their own consciousness and their actor voices match their personality very well.
I do not know if I should thank MangaGamer or LiarSoft or both for the vocabulary used in this game, but I have not read any profanity words during the MR AND in the sex scenes. About the sex scenes, I knew they were in this game – but they are soft and connected to the MR plot. I mean, there is not anything like “Hey, I like you, let’s have sex!” and all I could see was how strongly and deeply every character’s feelings for another one grew and how it ended in their first time (having sex, of course).
The point is, sex is not the focus of this VN, and it is only the consequence of the plot – and I was very surprised because of it. We have the girls’ act narrated so that all we can read is a beautiful poetry about their first time.
Above all, what impressed me the most was how focused on social aspects the game is. I mean, there are questions like “Do you think homosexuality is okay?” and “If I started dating a girl, how would society see us?”, what made me reflect about our own social values and everything – we can not deny that homosexuality is still a taboo in many countries.
I will finish my review here, because I do not want to give any spoilers or something like that. All I want to say is that if you are looking for a touching, beautiful and sensible game, KSotR is the right choice.

Death Rally is a top down racer made back in 1996 that has aged really well. You start with around $500 and a really bad car, and you must work your way up the ranks to become the best...yeah, no story. But it doesn't need one, as it lives and dies by it's gameplay.
You use machine guns, upgrades, new cars, and sabotoge? Yes, you can bribe mechanics to damage the best racers. You can also get rocket engines, spiked bumpers, and mines. You earn money from winning races, but you can get extra by doing certain tasks like killing all the opponets or not taking damage. You can also get hired to do things like killing a certain racer or getting "objects" and achieving first place (to hurry and deliver it...but wouldn't that draw too much attention if you get first place? whatever...). To start with the graphics they're great and have a nice blend of colors.And the crowd can smear blood trails if you hit them which is a nice touch(why are they on the track of a place called death Rally!?)though the tracks while they look good...some seemed to look the same with diffrent colors.
The sound is good. The machine gun sounds are great and the music is fine, but while it does it's job, it's not as dark as I thought it would be. Nice engine sounds as well. The controls are really tight and gets better with more upgrades.
The gameplay really shines here, with a great sensation of speed and the need to destroy your opponets, it just always feels intense every race. I really should mention you can turn off weapons...but that would ruin a lot of the fun,though it could be used to get the hang of the controls. Now the down sides are that, it can be grindy since you need cash to upgrade and get better in the races. You can NOT win without new cars and upgrades, and while that can be a turn off to some, it never made me feel like I was wasting my time. Not too much in the terms of replay value. Just multiple difficulty levels, though I had enough fun to want to play it again. Also the ending was anti-climatic. Not much beyond "You Win!" but I think the gameplay makes up for it.
overall 8/10 -If you want a good arcade-style racer with some edge, then this is what you want.

Dominique Pamplemousse reminded me of of the investigation portions in the Phoenix Wright games. It's the type of game where it's more of a visual novel, with not much in the way puzzles or logic tricks that you would expect from the average point-and-click adventure.  There are often moments where characters are having a conversation, and you are essentially just clicking the "next" button to hear the rest of it.
This is by no means a bad thing, though. A video game format can be used to deliver a story in a more nonlinear way that wouldn't be possible in any other medium. Just don't go in expecting much challenge.
The story itself actually had me pretty entertained and interested all the way through, with the twists and mysteries in the story being pulled off surprisingly well. There were also a few clever lines that ranged from making me smile to letting out a little chuckle.
I really enjoyed the musical element of the game. There's background music on each screen, and on some dialogue options, the characters will sing their lines in time with the music. The singing itself can be a little off-key at times, but I honestly enjoyed that. It added some charm. I'd really like to see the "singing along with the background music" done more in games. The background music is also really charming by itself, and I rather wish the soundtrack available for purchase would have included the instrumentals.
The game's description says it is a game about "gender and the economy", and while these subjects are touched on a few times, it's usually little more than a mention, and doesn't end up affecting the plot at much, which was a little disappointing. The game is really more about corporate intrigue and the music industry.
Dominique Pamplemousse is a fairly short game, clocking in at a little over an hour for me, and zero replayability, but for only five bucks, I would recommend it if you like mysteries and visual novels.

It's a pretty fun game, if you like(d) GTA and True Crime series. You get to be a thug and an undercover police-officer, and eventually you'll be trapped between these two roles. There are plenty of vehicles to try, relatively large area to explore and do missions in, and tons of people to beat up. Weapons are generally scarce, because (according to a game) it's Hong Kong, but as you advance further in the game, you'll be able to get access to them more and more. It's hard to recommend this game, but it's harder not to recommend it.
Street Fighter 5 is a skeletal game in its current state. There's very little single player content, and what is included is pretty terrible.
You don't play Street Fighter for the story... but if you're going to include a story mode it should be something more than 2-3 fight arcs with terrible anime-style slideshows in between. And the voice acting in the story mode? Heinous. Survival mode is a better way to waste time playing alone, but it works more as a distraction while waiting for an online match than as something you'd want to play for its own merits.
There are other things worth complaining about as well... even though a number of free additions are promised, you can already feel Capcom latching on to milk people with DLC. There's an in-game currency which will be usable in a forthcoming shop, but you it's already obvious that the game uses an initial dump of easy currency to get players excited, and then radically cuts down the earning pace so that people will feel incentive to spend real money on the ingame currency. It's not like Capcom is the only developer injecting "free to play" monetization into full priced products, but still... yuck.
All of that said - you should still play this game. The core fighting engine is the best of any Street Fighter game, and probably the best of *any* fighting game ever. It's crazy how fluid the game is, how inviting the controls are, and how intuitive each of the fighters feels.
Optimization on the PC is terrific - I'm running a graphics card which is just below the minimum recommended specs, and the game has no problem turning out 60FPS @ 720P/medium settings. The game looks terrific even at those curtailed settings - characters are huge and detailed, and animation is natural and smooth. I've seen some complaining about support/configurability for controllers, but i've experienced no problems; the game instantly recognized my old Madcatz xbox 360 fight pad and configured itself appropriately. Cross-play with people on Playstation also works without a hitch.
If you'll never play this game online, you should probably stay away - there just isn't much there for single player junkies. As a way to pummel the avatars of random strangers over the Internet, the game really has no equal. The feeling of a fierce punch connecting with your opponent's face is intoxicating... Humiliating (or being humiliated by) random people over the internet is really what life is all about, right?

See, the thing with visual novels on Steam is that they're either lacking in story, lacking in emotional pull (for me, at least), or they're het (again, that's a problem with me, others may vary). So, as it stands, it's kinda difficult to find a good yuri VN on here.
Kindred Spirits on the Roof exceeded my expectations. I swear on my own life, this is one of the best VNs I've ever plread. It has characters that you can connect with, who all have their own emotions and worries and traits. I felt myself get attached to each and every one of them, all in a different way. The romance is believable, shockingly enough for a VN, and the more intimate moments don't really feel forced. Quick note: If you're looking for "Oh girl-on-girl is hot" then I suggest you look elsewhere, because there are far better smut VNs for you to play in that case (I recommend Sono Hanabira for that).
I cried, I laughed, I smiled, I felt my face flush, I experienced more with this VN than I have...in a long while. Truly, one of the best I've played, and I am shocked to say that this surpasses Katawa Shoujo in my list of best VNs. This simply...hit me in a different way.
Now, that doesn't mean this VN is perfect. The music can be slightly annoying I suppose, but it didn't bother me all that much. Also, you might feel like the story repeats itself sometimes, since you go back through to see the couples outside of the main branch with Toomi.
Overall, I cannot recommend this enough, even at the price that it stands. 35 USD seems like a bit for a VN, but for quality...I feel quite confident in saying you won't find much better here on Steam.
Also, okonomiyaki is delicious, and I have this game to thank for sharing that with me.

Alright. So let’s get this started.
So, a simple announcement: This game does not have "steamy lesbian sex", as many people think. Nor is it a fluff “doki-doki magical girl” fest. At least not entirely. So if you want this game for either of those reasons, think twice.
Kindred Spirits, as a VL is really really nice. It's not a life changing game sure enough, but its filled with a good representation of "Girls Love" problems in a academic life style. I find the game long enough to expose and develop the whole story of the main characters and the different couples, and short enough you can play for a good amount of time without getting bored. (I know, it says I have about 5 hrs., but that’s because I had to run it outside steam. More on that later.)
KS has a solid and heart-warming story with interesting characters that develop nicely as the game goes on. No character ever becomes blurred in the sidelines, and they all have enough screen time and importance to be worthy of development. The game exposes several scenarios, each represented by a different girl, and by a different couple. Other than the 2 ghosts, the game is very faithful to (what I can imagine) realistic problems someone in that situation can have, without going too much on fantastic territory. Even the ghosts have problems that (if so the case") ghosts could have. Then again, I´m not a girl who fell in love with another girl, so...
All in all,  Kindred Spirits on the Roof is a medium-sized game with good exposure, heart-warming and hilarious situations, down to the ground thinking and reactions and interesting characters. If I had to say something bad, it would be that two certain situations are a bit to abrupt for certain characters.
Other than that, It´s a game that I fully recommend to anyone that wants to get started on Visual Novels, likes Yuri and has some spare time.
PROS:
-Interesting Characters
-Realistic plot
-Cute situations
-More Fluff than Sex
-When in Sex, well represented
-Complete and filling story
-A lot of in-depth to the characters.
CONS:
-Characters can be OOC at times
-Flat interface
-Steam version crashes the game every 15 mins or so. (To stop this, run the game outside of steam.)
Grade:
8.5/10

This is a fun and interesting little platformer. The controls are nice and fluid, the art style is a perfect match, and that narration! Most games, if you die, you get a simple "Game Over" screen, here, every single step you take, everything you do is part of the narration, so when you die, the narrator talks about it. That adds a levels of depth to the game that you don't see very often, without breaking the flow or seeming out of place.
The level designs are beautiful to see, with the ground literily being formed as you progress. The lack of fencing or borders along the edges is fine, since simply falling off the level doesn't kill you, and in some levels enemies will destroy ground tiles as they attack, making the fights get more challanging as they drag on.
An odd system here is that while there are only 2 difficulty levels to pick from at the start of the game (Normal and No Sweat), you can, after finding and building the Shrine, invoke differedn "Gods" to power up enemies in various ways. It's a novel system to let players tailor the challenge of the game to their liking, but unless you're really up for the challenge it really doesn't seem worth messing with on your first go through the game.
The only downsides I found here is that the game seems to lack a lot of replay value and, aside from the online leaderboards, there's not MP connectivity. Now, I haven't finished the game, but so far levels aren't replayable, which is annoying in case you missed something since you can't go back and get it one you complete that area. Also, levels don't seem to be randomized, so the layout may be fixed. Random levels that can be replayed after completing them would be a big plus for this game. As for the MP aspects, I know that not all games need an MP function or could even pull one off effectivly. However, if there was a kind of co-op or head-to-head function to this game, the replayability would go up.
As it stands Bastion is a great game with a fantastic story, wonderfully done visuals and solid platformer gameplay. The lack of much replay value hurts the game a little, but the Shrine mechanics can compensate for that to a small extent by letting you try the game with more and more powerful enemies. But while I still would have liked at least some kind of MP aspect outside the leaderboards, this game is well worth the price if you can get it on sale for -50% or more.

I honestly do't get all the hate towards this game. I love it. Sure, they could add some things/ work on some other stuff and I could cry about it, but I really enjoy what is already in here and wish I could find this in more RTS games. Let me, instead, respond to the negative reviews:
"Poor UI" (user interface): Coming from a huge fan of the original StarCraft which makes me very fond of the sequel, every time I go back to SC2 from SCFA or PA Titans, I feel like I've literally been shoved into a box. Zoom out from ground level to orbit and even the solar sytem. Not many games do this, but it is becoming a trend (which I am SO glad to see).
"Laggy": And it should be with how many units are in play across  the entire system. It's a demanding game and so is Ashes of the Singularity. Even then, I'm running a Skylake i5 6500 processor and 16Gb of DDR4 ram with NO, I repeat, NO graphics card and I only have issues when I go up against 10 bots. Upgrade your system or don't play against 10 bots or 15 players.
"I payed $90 and didn't get Titans for free": You "pledged" $90 to see this game come to life. Some people pledged and/or outright donated up to $250 and were happy with their decision. This should sum it up -
There are plenty like this thread if you Google it. Everyone wants the game for free at this point.
"The AI is dumb": Get a mod! There are so many people who back this game up and help create mods to make it even better! I personally went to them for issues when I first purchased the game and they are super friendly and helpful. And I personally find it hilarious when the AI kills itself (which happens to be rare, only 2 times so far, and possibly patched now).
"The Devs gave up on it": Not really. They're pretty busy with updates and future projects/games. I feel that Steam users like to throw this phrase around a lot more than it's needed.
All in all, if you are new to this franchise, I would highly recommend it. Well worth $40 in my opinion (though I did wait until it went on sale for $20 because I'm poor and shouldn't be buying games. lol) and I'll be looking forward to more games like this in the future.
*Update* I added a Radeon R7 370 graphics card from Sapphire with 4Gb of DDR5 ram and this game runs FLAWLESSLY with myself vs 9 AIs on the same team (spamming units on different planets and all)! I still don't understand how people get such bad lag with this game.

I've never written a review on here before, but for this VN, I simply have to. The shortest review I can possibly give would be one word: Masterpiece. However, I feel that such a short, generic review would not do this beautiful story justice. I also feel that it would be irresponsible of me to give spoilers to the plot, as it is best experienced for yourself as you play through the game, so instead, I will try to take the middle road between brevity and gushing over this wonderfully touching story.
For starters, if you are looking at this game simply because it is a yuri visual novel and you're expecting to get some good wank material out of it, you may want to move along. Yes, there are several sex scenes in the game. However, they are NOT written to entice or excite the reader. Rather, they are written realistically, in the perspective of the couples experiencing their first times together. They are not pornographic, but wonderfully, touchingly emotional.
The same can be said for the yuri romances throughout the game. They are not played up and fetishized, but are instead written in a sweet, pure way, genuinely fleshing out the feelings that the characters have for each other in a realistic way, as well as bringing up the worries of living in a traditional society that would see something wrong with them for feeling the way that they do.
All the characters are written fantastically, each having their own unique personalities, even if some of them do fall into some old character tropes from anime. There's the always sleepy (but surprisingly perceptive) Miyama Nena, the cuteness-obsessed Tsurigimine Kiri, and the air-headed, rock obsessed Koba Youka, to name just a few. While some of the characters seemed a little flat to me the first time they were introduced, the game does a fantastic job of fleshing them all out.
On top of the excellent writing, the soundtrack and cg are also top-notch. I did get a little annoyed with the fact that the music in the game doesn't loop, even though the majority of the music seems to be made in a way that it could loop. Instead of looping or stopping, it just fades out, then starts again from the beginning. However, this is a minor complaint, particularly when compared to the quality of the music itself. The cg for the characters and scenes is also fantastic, drawn very smoothly, but with just the slightest hint of sketchiness to the lines, giving it a sort of innocent feel that fits in with the overall tone of the game.
In short, if you're here because you have a fetish for yuri, don't bother. If you're here because you love love,  then pull up a chair, fork over 35 smackeroos, and get ready for a feels trip straight to YURITOPIA!

Downsides
1) It's occasionally buggy, though improved from what it used to be like.  On occasion a mission will start with a white map for me, but a quick restart of the game generally sorts it with no gameplay lost.
2) It can also become a bit monotonous if you let it—it's up to you to be creative in your gameplay to keep yourself interested.  But this can be said of many RTS games.
Overall, I would definitely recommend playing.

This originally started off as a browser game, which proved to be such a hit with the people who played it, that they wanted to help support the creators to get onto Steam and Mobile - so it could become more well known. With a successful kickstarter and greenlight, the goal was finally achieved! Perhaps in the future it will make it to other platforms, too.
Don't let my time here fool you. I have just a little over a thousand matches played at this point in time from the browser version. So, where to begin?
Well, first off, this is a party game based on the likes of Mafia. It's played with up to fifteen people, though you wouldn't want to have any less in order to have the best kind of game. The current updated version of this game starts you with the ability to choose your name – which can result in some hilarious trolling, depending on your mood. You know something's happening when half of the players decide to call themselves after Game of Thrones characters, or someone has a name that automatically makes others hate them.
After that, you have the role-wheel, which will select you your role for the game. This can be skewed in favour of those who have brought scrolls from the in-game shop to try and increase their chances of landing the role they want. For example, every role can have a 7% chance of being selected for you. If you use a scroll, it can increase the odds of the role you want to say, 20%, whilst decreasing the odds for everyone else – so they would drop from 7% to 4%. This can be annoying if you prefer to not obtain scrolls – but honestly, there is so many roles to choose from, it shouldn't matter too much. At some point, you will have roles you don't want, and roles you love. That's part of the fun of a randomised selection. The shame about this is that you will get pop up adds to entice you into the shop to buy things.
After finding out which of the 33 roles you are, you then act as according to it for the game. Each game can be anything between ten to thirty minutes long. The main game is split into several phases. You start off with:
Day One: discussion. Then night one. Then day two: Deaths. Then discussion. Then voting. Then discussion – this cycle repeats right up until the ultimate winner(s) are declared. Depending on your role, will depend on when you can preform your actions – if you have actions to achieve. With the voting phrase, if someone is voted up, they have to defend themselves, and the other players will vote guilty or innocent. Guilty votes will kill the defendant, and innocent ones will spare them.
You have three “sides” to speak of. Side one is town, or the “good” side. Town's main job is to oust the bad side before the bad side kills them. The catch is, Town has no clue who is Town and who isn't. So through discussion and usage of roles, they have to work out who is telling the truth and who is lying. You can get Support roles, Protective roles, and killing roles.
Side two is Mafia, the “bad” side. Mafia's main job is to kill every town member and persuade them all the while that they're Town. Mafia's average number is three. Their advantage over Town is that the Mafia know who each other is, and can communicate with each other at night. You can get Deception roles, Support, and Killing.
Side three is Neutrals, who all have individual goals that can either tie hand in hand with Town or Mafia, or just benefit themselves. You can get Benign neutrals, Killing neutrals, or just plain Evil ones.
Because there are so many roles, I will just mention around two from each “side” as a small example of the kinds you can get.
One role Town can get is an Investigator. During night-time, they can choose to look at another player to determine what role they have. A successful invest will reveal up to three roles the person can be. For example, someone could show up as Vigilante (Town Killing), a Veteran (Town Killing) or a Mafioso (Mafia Killing.) Through guesswork and questions, you can figure out if the person is good or not. Another town role is the Jailer. At daytime, they can choose to jail whoever they think is suspicious, or someone random. At night, they can then question the person in their jail to try and figure their role out. If the Jailer suspects their captive of lying, then they can choose to execute them.
For the Mafia, they can have a Godfather, who is the leader. He can kill someone at night, or make a Mafioso do it for them. Their advantage is that they can't be killed at night, so if someone shot them, they would be immune. The Disguiser for Mafia is someone who can take on the name, position, and face of someone who died. So if a confirmed Town player is chosen to be killed, the Disguiser can choose to “become” that Town, and people would believe they were still the same player.
For Neutrals, you can get an Jester, whose goal is to be hung by everyone else. They can do this by being annoying or throwing false information. If they are hung, they can choose to kill a guilty voter at night, from the graveyard. You can also get a Serial Killer, whose goal is to kill everyone – Town and Mafia. Serial Killers are also immune at night.
So, yes. There's a lot of roles. But really, the main selling point of this game is not the graphics, the music, or the diversity of the roles. It's the interaction with other players. Every single game is different because it depends on each player's ability to successfully do their role, and convince others of the truth, or their lies. It's a game about deception, and the feeling you can get when you pull off a tricky deception is just amazing. Imagine the Town's surprise when you convince them you're just a poor doctor who wants to heal people – and actually turn out to be the Serial Killer. Poor things. Maybe there's not a lot of good to be said about a game that teaches you how to lie convincingly, but trust me. This is fun!
A very important things players need to do is write their findings or information down in their last wills. That way, if they die, the information can be read by everyone else, and hopefully benefit whoever needs the information the most. (For example, an investigator may have found the Godfather, but isn't sure, so they write it down. And when they die, people can see they suspected someone of being a Godfather.)
You'll get people who leave if things don't go their way, or people who game throw, so quite a few times, a game will depend on the personalities of those you interact with. I've had some frustrating games where people ruin it for others, and awesome games where everyone is doing what they should be doing – and injecting a little fun into it, too.
I honestly think everyone should try this game at some point. It's free as well since it's still browser based. I chose to buy the game here because I loved it, and wanted to support BlankMediaGames. You have absolutely nothing to lose from trying this game out. And if you play with friends, you may end up damaging friendships, but that's okay. They'll forgive you … in time.
Go play!

Where to start...
This game is for the explorers and base builders. The combat is a ton of fun and is very well balanced, but I feel like the best part of this game is exploring planet after planet and spending hours in the mines imo. The bosses are quite difficult, however they become exponentially less difficult with even one other player present. Save for the Vault bosses, they're a scary pain in the backside always, but in a fun challenging way.
There is a LOT of variety in the weapons and armor, and you never know what you will find in chests and vendors. The random generation makes the weapons (especially the ranged weapons) as unique as everything else in the game. That being said, there are still items that aren't randomly generated, such as certain weapons you craft and rare unique weapons, but they definitely don't dissapoint either. Especially the unique weapons. I have yet to get bored of anything in this game, and I've been playing it since its super early days of early access.
If you are a builder, explorer, and/or collector, I highly recommend this game. The game has a pretty good story too, so if that's your thing, I'd recommend at least trying it. The best part of this game is that content and feature updates are stilll rolling out, so I have no doubts that this game will continue to become even more awesome than it already is in the future. Definitely, definitely try this game out.
TL;DR This game is friggin awesome, so at least give it a try. I highly recommend it.

This review is more of an argument and is long, but in my opinion, is necessary. I have always enjoyed the Fallout universe. Its vast lore, storyline, content, and immersion are just a few of the amazing qualities that this series has to offer.
My arguments against negative reviews:
1. Paid mods and dlc do not destroy the game. I know multiple people that have played this game, time and time again, never using mods or dlc, and have enjoyed it immensely. Furthermore, paid mods and dlc are around in a wide variety of games, and are not that uncommon. They aren’t a signature feature of Fallout 4. They do not destroy the overall game, especially because of the quality this and other games have to offer nowadays, and especially because buying mods and dlc is a choice.
2. The FPS feeling of Fallout 4 was its intended style. This FPS style was the style that the developers intended for this game to play as. It was meant to feel like you were struggling to survive, having to fend off enemies everywhere and anywhere. Moreover, play style still varies. You can play as both a sneak character, as well as an aggressive character. You can be a sniper, as well as a melee character. The play style varies, as it was intended, and as it should. Unlike Fallout and Fallout 2, this game, in its 3D style, is intended to be played similar to an FPS, so I don’t exactly understand the point of this negative argument. Skyrim would be the exact same way, if it had guns.
This game is an amazing game, plays as it’s supposed to be played, and being a AAA game, isn’t destroyed by the optionally-purchased mods and dlc it has to offer.

Fun, addicting, old-school MMORPG. The comparisons to classic Runescape are unavoidable; however, RPG MO avoids paywalls and offers more overall content. While RPG MO is listed as "Early Access" on Steam, the game has been public since 2012. (I have >100 hours played via Steam, but I almost always play using a web browser--my actual play time is >1000 hours for sake of review.)
Pros:
+ 18 different skills to level.
+ no hard level cap and very high soft-cap.
+ lots of content.
+ open world sandbox.
+ micro-transactions are available for purchasing some items; however, this ultimate just offers a method to get coins slightly faster. No true advantage for those that support the game.
+ fantastic (best I have seen) communities.
Cons:
- some may not like the very grindy nature.
- some may not like losing most items in their inventory when dying (avoiding death is very easy).
- limited partying with other members; this is a major opportunity for future development.
You will see some complain about the chat moderators; the rules are very clear, and the chat moderators are very strict about the rules around the default chat channel (EN - RPG MO). As long as you do not curse and follow the most basic of rules (no off-topic in channel EN), you will never have an issue.
Development is always ticking away. It may be slower than some indie games, but it is definitely faster than most. The only way I see development rate being a complaint is just by the opportunities around partying and end-game content.

Street Fighter V has its ups and downs, but sadly in its current state, I can't recommend the game until the issues have been resolved. - Graphics are rich and colorful
Cons:
- The netcode is absolutely awful

A simple yet deep action game that plays well depending on your choice of controls
Upon first look into this top-down action game I was compelled to report that this was a simple game with simple mechanics, simple game play and a simple story.  Not soon after I completed the first area did I come to the understanding just how much depth was contained within this game despite the simplicity of the mechanics.  Bastion truly is an experience to be had despite its unorthodox art-style, soundtrack and narrative.  Like many games of the indie genre, it is a refreshing break away from the mainstream but still contains the clean and somewhat polished look of many mainstream action titles that holds a place for both casual and competitive gamers.  This title is not without its quirks but contains a wholly unique experience that drives players from area to area.
The story of Bastion is one of hope and survival.  Though not being terribly deep, the story is able to propel players from each area to the next.  It is not one given to gamers in a mainstream way.  It comes to players as if they are hearing a story given from the perspective of a  soothing-voiced supporting character.  Though the narrative was told in a story-like fashion, I never felt like it forgot about what was happening on the screen.  It was interactive and reacted to what my character was doing in the various areas.
The story tells of the Calamity, a single apocalyptic even that lays waste the land and has released many monsters to impede your progress.  Few people remain and those that you find on your journey join you at the Bastion, a safe haven and the future of your people.  You begin your journey as a boy that has just awoken to find the effects of the Calamity and is being lead by the narrative to the Bastion.  You begin to rebuild the Bastion that will save the world and must traverse many hostile areas to find crystal shards that give the Bastion core power to rebuild.  On your journey you meet just a few characters that add depth to the story.  They merely give information and are not intended to physically aid you in your journey.  They story unfolds into one of treachery and deceit and has you make a few very difficult decisions as you approach the end of the game.  Though initially surface level, the story become one that some players may become emotionally engaged in.  Overall, the story is great and the experience is solid.
When it comes to game play in Bastion simplicity is the name of the game.  Everything from the controls to the mechanics scream simplicity.  This is not to be confused with the game being simple however.  There were many instances where I began slapping keys out of frustration on a particularly difficult segment of the game.  The top down action genre has generally been associated with games like old school Grand Theft Auto and Diablo, but Bastion brings a more hack n' slash element to the genre with its various weapons and real time action.  Initially there are just the basic moves such as the primary and secondary weapon actions.  There are simple dodge and defend mechanics as well.  However not far down the path you begin to realize that there are many seemingly trivial elements introduced during the opening area that are absolutely crucial to be successful in the following areas.  I was pleasantly surprised to come to an area where I was to only surpass by timing counter attacks perfectly or practice efficiency with a weapon by only being allowed a certain amount of shots.
Bastion is not without its quirks however.  Having the PC title allowed me to choose whether I wanted to use the keyboard and mouse or a game pad.  I was able to try both as I had an old Xbox360 controller lying around.  After some time and a sideways expression, I came to find that depending on the weapons you chose to utilize on your journey, your choice of input greatly decided the difficulty or simplicity of the game.  I found that using a mouse an keyboard was more difficult because you had to manually aim shots whereas the game pad had a lock-on feature.  I also found that navigating the world of Bastion was much more intuitive with a game pad.  However, the keyboard and mouse offered much greater ease when it came to using weapons that had area of affect damage because I could aim at a group as opposed to an individual enemy.  Overall, the game pad was easier to use on a far greater range of weapons.  In the end, I ended up using both my keyboard and mouse and the game pad.  This I felt was a quirk that could have been resolved by implementing an auto-aim feature on either input device that could be turned on or off on the fly.  The would have prevented the need to sometimes constantly switch input devices.  If a player has the Xbox360 version of the game, they are most definitely limited to using just a game pad as the Xbox360 does not support mouse input.
I feel that Bastion is a very unique experience that anyone can enjoy.  It allows users to merely play a decently designed game or get engaged into the story.  It does so many things well that its easy to overlook its input quirks.  It allows for gamers of all skills and gives an engaging 4-6 hour experience.

I'm starting to see a lot of unwarranted negativity around this game. I started playing pretty early on and have been here each update. The devs have been putting a lot of work into this game since it started in early access and the updates were farely frequent and added new stuff as well as fix old stuff. This game is awesome, one of my favourite rts' even. The idea of having multiple planets in an rts has ruined me. I just wish other games incorporated scale like this. But keep in mind that this isn't an amazing rts by most people standards. The game itself is pretty simple so the only difficulty is in managing the scale of the battle. You'll be warring over planets, fighting for control over moons and the metal planet for huge tactical advantages (slamming or blasting a hole in your oponents planet). It's not easy to play but it is crazy and when you get used to it it's really fun.
Now for the controversy...
They released a dlc pack for the game which really did add a lot to the game (A lot of new units and titans mostly). But the problem (if you can call it one) is that this pack is a stand alone dlc. What that means is that if you buy the dlc, you get the entire game plus the dlc (This was the only way to get the dlc, Now you can buy the base game and the dlc is dlc)). I bought this game for about $45 on a steam sale and I got the dlc for $10. Now when you consider that I technically got a new game for $10 it really isn't a problem. Sure my friends didn't want to get the expansion but guess what, I just play the base game with them because thats what they have. Even if this weren't standalone NOTHING would be any different. So despite what you may read in other reviews, this game is great, the devs worked hard, and "Titans" was never a problem.
I strongly recommend this game to anyone who likes rts games because it really brings a lot of new stuff to the genre. It's not the best rts out there but what it tries to do, it does well enough to be enjoyable at least casually.

A very interesting game. A bit rought around the edges, but there is a lot to enjoy and to be admired here. Clearly a passion project, it plays out like a murder mystery on a space ship with an impressive amount of outcomes and ways to handle it. If you're going the completionist route, you will be playing this for hours. I did enjoy the variety I could approach situations and interact with the people, and I found it fun to just talk to the people on board the ship.
The combat is.. rough, but it works. A bit unforgiving in the sense, that you can die quite easily, but the combat isn't the main meat here in the least. There is a surprising amount of variety to the combat in the way that there is first-person shooting with various weapons, an inventory system, and sometimes even a turret minigame thing, which was quite refreshing.
I will be following this series, and Consortium: The Tower is certainly something I will want to look into in the future, as the game ends on quite the cliffhanger, which already did heaps to sell me on the sequel, which seems to be in early access as of typing. The trailers for the sequel already show improved combat mechanics (along with vertical movements solutions), and the only bad thing I can really say about this game, is that the combat is very rough.
Overall, I would recommend this game, as it was a pleasant surprise and a worthwhile experience.

Zone 4 on Steam will be remembered as the perfect way on how to not bring back a dead MMO.
Originally an asian MMO from Korea I believe, it was eventually brought to the west through the same company that held other similar MMO fighting games, and things were good for a while. It seemed to be a thriving game back then but it was flawed, specifically in the way you leveled up skills using Skill Strengthening & Superior Skill Strengthening Coupons. Let's just say it was enough to give you PTSD with those damn things. It had a reliable, not too expensive cash shop with enough stuff to make anyone happy. However this was not to last as it was announced that the servers would get shut down. The only place left where the game was still thriving was in Brazil ( of all places ) until it's eventual demise as well.
Fast forward to a year or so back when it was announced that they wanted to greenlight Zone 4 on steam. A lot of old Zone 4 fans flocked to get it through and it did.
The first sign of problem was that it was delayed for sometime ( a week? I don't remember ).
The second sign was that once in the game, the new cash shop was ludicrously expensive. Things that, before had costed say maybe 1$ was now 10$. And then there was the whole upgrade skills system that had been revamped... for the worse. I don't even remember how it was handled in the steam version but I think you had to invest money into it.
Aside from these problems, there was also the problems on the forums - People being outright hostile towards Brazilian people, and others complaining about the server issues regarding that Europeans had crap latency. Being European myself, I can't really say I experienced that bad of a latency issue, but there was some issues certainly. They never fixed this of course.
So to recap:
- Very expensive Cash shop.
- Latency Issues.
- Significantly worsened skill upgrade system.
- Lack of care from Infovine.
They clearly showed that they had learned nothing from why Zone 4 died before.
I remain convinced that this resurrection on steam was solely to line their own pocket with money.
The game remained online for about five to six months.
And then, it died again. A shame really.

This is the best open world game that Bethesda Game Studio has produced so far, in my opinion. The world is hugely interactive and filled with events and npc interactions to discover even without doing quests. There are many interesting quests not connected to the main story line. It is an exploration heaven. Where does this road go, where do these tracks lead, where did that explosion come from, what just zoomed overhead and appeared to crash over there etc. This is a great fire arms combat game and simultaneously the most *advanced* RPG game produced to date. The two are not incompatible as you will happily find out. You are not just a passive roller of dice waiting to see how some previous stat choice will play out. It puts you (the actual player) in the action along with your avatar and you decide which challenge to accept now or save for later when better prepared. It is so much more advanced and immersive than an obsolete virtual score pad and dice. Modern RPG lovers can leave all of that to grandpa now.
All of the optional companions are unique quests unto themselves and can be manipulated by your decisions and actions while with them to grow to hate you or to love you unconditionally.  Finding out which actions inspire love or hate is part of the fun and each companion is different. In addition most have interesting unique quests attached to them which you can discover by taking them on each in turn.
There are a set number of settlement locations that you may optionally build up and maintain. Waiting for you within the main quest line is a quest giver which will help you find all of the settlement locations but all of those locations can be found independently by exploring this living world all on your own. The problems of creating each settlement are the same for each but the geography of each site poses a unique challenge and requires your special input to solve.  The possible solutions that can be brought to this problem are literally endless. It is a new and genuine RPG feature with which no other RPG to date can compete.
The game has hundreds upon hundreds of hours of content making for an enormous value per cost of entertainment at full price or even higher.  If your IQ is above room temperature and your hardware is above required specs you will not experience 'game stopping bugs'.  You do not need any mods but there are a huge number available *for free* right from the game menu if you wish. If you want to engage in the now enormous number of mods for this game be sure to get all of the DLC because all of it is used by those mods.
Ignore the current wave of hate being politically coordinated against the publisher for the Creation Club. It has no bearing at all upon your potential enjoyment of this brilliant game. It is simply the bleating of a minority of childish sheep who think that the world owes them a living. That will change for them when they make their first insurance payment and pay their first income tax bill.
