A text review is provided below-
Consortium is a first person RPG. It’s a very unique game that’s for sure. It has RPG elements, shooting mechanics, and quite easily the most impressive conversation simulations I have seen in my entire life. The buttons for conversations however are in the F keys like F1 and F2, so that’s a little odd and has led to the occasional mis-click on my part that had...undesirable results. But honestly, I have never seen a game more capable of having the most realistic and intelligent conversations as Consortium. The shooting mechanics are solid, AND entirely optional. You never once have to shoot a gun in this game if you don’t want to.
Consortium is a very choice-driven game. Every action you make, everything you say and do has a reaction. You can play this game as a pacifist, as a rambo, or as someone just trying to survive or what have you if you wish. The gameplay is very solid and a definite pro in my book. You can even explore the plane through all the maintenance corridors above and below where you’re supposed to be just like in Star Trek or that one scene in Mass Effect 2, it’s really cool the first time you discover it.
The story of Consortium is an interesting one. It’s essentially one big murder mystery with some extra things happening. You have to use the in-depth conversation mechanics and your own ingenuity to discover why the casualty was murdered and who was behind it. It’s actually pretty awesome, and I HATE murder mysteries. The reason I think it is so awesome is probably because I’m a huge fan of Star Trek and seeing as all of this takes place on a futuristic plane that is essentially a flying fortress that can laser zap missiles and planes out of the air by the hundreds... It’s sort of like you’re playing through your own episode (Which is a very good point I saw another review make)...except you’re not in command. But that’s good, I mean, I wouldn’t be able to have half of the humorous reactions I had in this game if I were supposed to be the always-busy all-feared “captain” of the plane.
The graphics are decent. The voice acting is actually pretty great. There’s some voice acting that might be considered mediocre but I loved it either way. The sounds themselves were alright I suppose. Nothing memorable there but nothing particularly bad either.
But this game must have a con right? As all games do. Yes. This game has one gigantic glaring con that is so bad that it actually caused me to walk away from my computer mid-playthrough. This game has the big glaring RPG-cancer of an issue where continuing the primary questline makes you fail all of the side quests. But that on its own isn’t bad. The fact that they don’t TELL you about this game-ruining feature if you don’t save enough that most RPGs were done with ten years ago is bad. ANd unless you intentionally stop playing for a minute to look for what’s what you have NO idea what’s a primary objective and what isn’t unless you paid attention to the two second pop up when you receive an objective (which usually comes mid-dialogue). There is no quest tracking of any kind so if you’re just playing to play immersively as the game so encourages, you might accidentally trigger THAT phase in the main quest where all of your side quests are canceled. This usually happens after 10 minutes of dialogue meaning that if you reload a save to make sure you don’t ♥♥♥♥ that up, you have to sit through 10 minutes of the same dialogue AGAIN. Looks like realistic conversations has a con. Maybe if paired with realistic time progression though, it wouldn’t be as bad. This is all very critical in my opinion though because these side quests are, with the exception of one, all VERY closely linked to the main story which is essentially the investigation on the murder. Then there’s some minor issues as well like strange delays in loading screens and the issue of being a floating head with no body that so many first person games mess up, but nothing quite as glaring as the ability to ♥♥♥♥ up your progression without so much as a notice that THAT is what doing THAT particular quest will do.
So my final rating for Consortium is a 6/10. I think in itself it is definitely a good game, but this design choice alone ruins my entire view on the game. If you know about it in advance, it’s not that bad. But if you’re unfortunate enough to start this game without knowing that this is a FEATURE? Then it could be enough to convince you to put the game down. It’s a short game. You already experienced half of it by the first point you can get ♥♥♥♥ed over. What’s the point in continuing? It’ll just be more of the same.
So do i recommend Consortium? Well, yes and no. I’m going to state officially no because I don’t believe in supporting a game that makes design choices that were bad enough when they were invented but then makes them years after seemingly every other RPG developer caught on and stopped making that flaw of a design choice. BUT, the thing is so long as you are willing to break the immersion to look up every story situation you come upon to see if this is a “no-return” type of thing and avoid primary objectives at all costs should you not find a clear answer? Then it’s actually a really a good game. Very unique and something we need to see more of. So while I don’t recommend this for anyone who just wants a stress-free good game to play. I do recommend it for those that want an interesting game and are willing to go out of their way to stop the game from screwing them over.

Yuritopia!
But really, this game is great.
Yuritopia- I mean, Kindred Spirits on the Roof is a mainly kinetic visual novel (meaning that choices, if any, have almost no effect on the outcome of the story) in which Toomi Yuna, a 2nd year highschooler encounters a ghostly couple on the roof of her school. She quickly becomes their (slightly unwilling) accomplise in bringing other girls in her school together.
In order of best to worst from my experience:
Art: 10/10
I havent seen a game of any kind in so long where the artist actually took the effort to make different costumes and colors for a whole variety of situations. In particular, I love the style <3. It really helps to bring to mind the feeling of a girl in love.
Music: 9/10
The track isn't very large, but what is there is well made and pleasant to listen to without being too overwhelming or distracting. Only problem I really had was that the tracks didn't loop at all.
Story: 8/10
The premise of the plot is actually...kind of orginal? It definitely wasn't something I'd seen before. Of course, in execution, the story became a little more mundane, but it was still enticing to read from beginning to end, and I loved the ending.
Characters 7/10
Most of the characters are well developed, but they tend towards fairly typical archetypes common in japanese culture, so if you're used to that, you might get bored of their antics quickly.
As for stuff that can't easily be graded:
+ Game length: for me, I cleared the main story in about 20 hours, but there's more for you to do afterwards, and I estimate about atleast another 5-8 hours of gameplay is left. Not bad at all.
- UI: While the UI is not cluttered, It is instead compact and fairly complicated for a VN, including far more visual buttons than is common. On that note, the options is fairly cluttered, even if everything is labeled.
All in all, I think the game is almost worth its full price, which is not something I'd say about most VN's, especially on steam. Even at 10% off, I think this game is worth buying.
TL;DR : 11/10 would yuritopia again

A game has almost nine-year history, but unfortunately something remains the same. It is fun only if there is balance, but that exists like in the beginning when everything just started. A game has been run several times by different companies already and now another publishing for almost three months, the player base dropped and is still slowly decreasing. According to its record, hope this time it will be lasting longer before shutting down.
The fighting system is definitely a rip-off of Urban Reign, a Namco game on PS2 released in 2005. Zone4 seems to appeal to more potential customers, so violence behavior is a bit reduced, and the pace is slower than Urban Reign. Somehow, certain handy features are not implemented like targeting on a specific opponent. Without this, confronting multiple enemies nearby may lead you to attack one which you unintentionally target.
Fighting movements of eight classes are highly inspired by famous fighting games, for example, Tekken, Virtua Fighter and Urban Reign, of course. In my opinion, most of them are the same animation yet crudely made.
There are three major modes, Hunting Ground & Arcade like Beat'em up games, PvP and Zombie Defense. Despite that, none of them are played often, at least, publicly.
To get survive in this game, good and high-level items and skills are required. With them, a player can advance to a better state, probably. However, problems are everything is based on luck, which is too strictly rare to happen when farming and upgrading. Without fair luck, there is no chances to acquire better gear. Without better gear, farming is painful. because of these, hunting ground is crossed out. Arcade is paid low, and the rewards of Zombie Defense even got nerfed. What's worse, all of them are limited in times to enter per day. Hunting Ground gives a player 30 minutes to hang around every time.
PvP is what gives players more fun to stay and much more gaming experience, although there is some flawed unbalance between classes which are never fixed. All entertainment vanishes after becoming level 20 or above. A few hits by OP players and downs are the situation an ordinary player is going to face. Personal skill and experience won't work much against them when the difference of ability values between you and them is so huge, and also the delay makes it like rock-paper-scissors when dodging.
Items purchased via the microtransaction are either too expensive or frustrating Gacha eggs which are usually timed.
The biggest deal in this game is, that stuff only available for people who pay real cash, which makes them earn Zen faster and easily. These items can only be accessed by them. As time goes by, the gap is getting even huge, making this game much harder for normal ones and of course, unfriendly to newcomers.
Conclusion, Game is based on good luck, paid for much better luck, unclear and unfriendly guides for starters, consists of unfair and unbalanced competition and glitches lying there for a long time. Game is potential fun, lots of selection for classes, but for a PvP game, which is still requiring some skill, it becomes a fail with the flaws and unbalance.
For return players, give a try and enjoy the old time and memories then.
For people who are new to it, I suggest wasting no time and cash. Honestly, this is just like a recycled game. There are thousands of far more interesting and cheaper games on Steam, whose developers deserve your courage and money.
If you really enjoy this type of fighting controls, go get Urban Reign to play with your friends.

The artwork, character controls, interface and general stability (on PC) are obviously much better than The Sandbox, but it doesn't quite capture the magic of the past game.
In particular the temperature system isn't as well balanced. It's easier to get a runaway temperature reaction (eg dropping one ice in a body of water and forming a glacier). You could do that in the previous game, but the ice was much more likely to melt if you only dropped one, and it was easier to erase all the ice and get your water back. In this game temperature tends to stick around and you typically have to erase a lot of the surrounding solid blocks in order to get
non-freezing temperatures back.
It's also a lot less system oriented than the previous game. As an example, lasers in this game are simply 1 block that you place and they work as lasers. There's a block for every different kind of mirror. In the previous game a laser was a laser block, some glass blocks to determine the direction of the laser, (optionally, a gem for different laser effects - no gems in this game yet). Then you placed different kind of mirrors by placing glass blocks in certain patterns.
Even so, I love the Sandbox and the Sandbox Evolution is almost as good, so I also love Sandbox Evolution. It still has the temperature, weather and electronics system, in fact most of the systems from the Sandbox are in Evolution.

As a fan of hidden object games I jump into each one with a sense of excitement and hope, sometimes the game delivers and sometimes it doesn’t. I found
to be very middle of the road. It had a nice look, nice puzzles and hidden object scenes but lacked an engaging story. This title is one of six currently available on Steam by Brave Giant LTD, so far I’ve played five of these titles and found most to be mediocre. It wasn’t until I played this game the second time that I really noticed it. However, being mediocre doesn’t make this title bad.
The story is set during World War II, you play as Agent Walker, who has been sent on a mission to find a powerful artifact so that the enemy doesn’t get to it first. This MacGuffin is the Spear of Destiny -reputed to be the weapon that killed Jesus Christ, ending his agony on the crucifix.  Some legends declared its wielder became ruler of the world.  It ends up falling into enemy hands as you could imagine and you spend most of the game trying to track it down and destroy it. That’s pretty much all the story is about. Agent Walker is never given any development, she’s a total placeholder for the player with little personality. Despite being set during World War II there is never a huge sense of dread or urgency about anything, this could have easily been set during any war on any planet with the same outcome. There also isn’t much of a supernatural element to the game, there is a brief explanation about the spear given to you during a mini game and not much else. I did find the title to have a decent sense of action though as you do move around often and explore quite a few locations.
What I enjoyed most was the gameplay here, there are plenty of hidden object scenes and puzzles to keep you entertained. The game starts off strong, adding some rarely seen variety to the usual hidden object scenes but that dies off around midway through and they all end up being the usual list of objects you have to find. The scenes do offer morphing objects, this is when an item you need to find continually morphs into another object so you have to keep an eye out when to click on it. The puzzles were enjoyable, most weren’t too difficult at all. There were some fun ones like parachuting and even driving a boat which I don’t often see as well some of the staples you tend to find in this genre. You’re given a map that shows you where an action can be performed and also allows you to teleport, as well as three different difficulty settings and a custom setting.
Visually the game performs well. While some of the animations of the characters might seem a bit stiff, everything looks pretty good. It feels like the 1940’s and like it’s set during a war. The hidden object scenes are done well, the items aren’t hard to see or blurry and overall everything is very clean. The audio, on the other hand, is a mixed bag. Most of the voice acting is pretty lackluster. Some characters speak like robots almost, most are just middle of the road and Agent Walker herself never speaks at all. Voice acting isn’t required, but if you choose to add it, then it should be enjoyable to the ear. Thankfully the music is alright and fits well with the tone and setting of the game.

During World War II, a course to retrieve the mythical Spear of Destiny, destined to help people rule the world, is happening between Axis and Allies. Agent Walker is sent to destroy it after it was localized in France. However, once there, she fell in a trap...
The Spear of Destiny... it's not the first time that I've heard about it: another casual adventure game has the same object in a similar setting and I still remember that a similar artifact was one of the objectives of Lara Croft in Chronicles.
Agent Walker is another twist: while the Spear is found early, Nazis managed to retrieve it as she fell into a trap. The result is the chase through a village and underground temples. However, the Spear of Destiny isn't the only thing: there is a colossus you need to finish as it's protecting the Spear and the machine that can destroy it is situated elsewhere. Some twists are also present, though I would have preferrd more interaction with enemies and more explanations on the twist.
However, Agent Walker is pretty standard on the gameplay: hidden objects scenes to clear (relatively easy, though some items are changing appearance), puzzles (also easy), find items, combine them, use them to advance. This is more of a first impression than a review, considering my limited play time.
I completed the tutorial and set about trying to get started, but found myself struggling against the game's UI and controls, which aren't at all intuitive. The added step of requiring a tool to be equipped in order to perform a function makes the experience feel fiddly, and I feel that a better alternative would be to simply require the tool to be in inventory instead of constantly having to switch.
Failure rates for resource gathering seem to be on the high side. Frequent failures left me wondering if I was doing something wrong. I understand that success is tied to skill, which is a good idea in theory, but might be better represented by allowing higher skill levels to instead have a chance to gather multiple items from succeeding.
Combat seems to be a simple case of your stats versus the enemy's, as once you click on them, automated turns with what I'm assuming are background dice rolls decide how much damage you deal/recieve. That's fine for what it is, as the game seems to focus as much on the gathering/crafting system as combat. Still, this gives you very little influence on the outcome of any given battle aside from what stats you decided to train via the use of combat stances.
I think the game looks nice in its own way. They're definitely going for a specific style here and it's represented up front. If you hate it, there's a good chance you're not even reading this review.
In general, I guess the main reason I'm not recommending this game is because there doesn't seem to be anything particularly unique here. It wears its influences on its sleeve, and it's a fine "one of those games." Problem is, it hasn't improved or iterated upon those influences, and in fact lags behind them in some areas.
If none of what I said has swayed you, then you might as well give it a try. I wanted to put this out there to try and save people some time, but considering the lack of a price tag, time is all you've got to lose by giving this game a shot.

Consortium is quite a unique game. Imagine if Deus Ex and Star Trek had a baby. Do NOT play this game expecting anything from the combat other than Deus Ex without all the special abilities and augmentations (And Deus Ex's combat is nothing to brag about in itself). However this game surpasses both Deus Ex and Bioware titles like Mass Effect when it comes to the flow of the narrative. Because the narrative is so short and focused (about two hours max per playthrough) you will feel like you are in an episode of Star Trek because the story never lets up, there is no time time or break in the narrative, just pure plot while you get to know the characters over the two hours you will spend with them (or more, for additional playthroughs).
You take the role of Bishop 6, a member in the Consortium whose ranks are made up like ranks on a Chess Board with everything above pawns basically being the officers. The game takes place on an airplane but absolutely feels like a Starship with crew quarters, a bridge and a "view screen" encounter right out of Star Trek. If you're a fan of Star Trek you can think of your place in the narrative as a sort of cross between Commander Riker and Lieutenant Worf. Being a fan of Star Trek is not required but you will find additional enjoyment in the narrative if you are.
Pros:
The characters, the branching storyline and the amount of voice work. The last one in particularly makes this game stand out and it is constantly taken for granted- From start to finish you go through several plot narratives and will come to expect the constant communications of officers on the crew due to the large amount voice content that is in this game, the story never stops so why should the characters. A large amount of games either fail in this regard or fail to truly take advantage of what a large amount of voice work (actually pertaining to the plot) can do
This game's weakest point is easily the combat, I honestly recommend putting the difficulty on easy and cruising through because the combat is there to represent two types of choices (Fight/Not Fight and Lethal/Non-Lethal) and it serves it's purpose for that but nobody is going to play this solely for the combat. I personally can no longer take a FPS game with guns seriously unless it has ADS (aim-down-sight) but that's just me. The "guns" in this game feel lousy, shoot lousy and hit lousy. The second weakest point is that if you make it to the end of the game, it will leave you wanting more (which is a good thing, and a sequel is on the way). If the developers could find a way to make this game episodic in nature and roll out content on a regular basis they would really be on to something especially with the branching storylines and character relationships involved. There are also a few bugs here and there and you will more than once catch characters "miming" at you like they are working a computer in thin air (could MAYBE be explained by some kind of augmented reality system... but that's a stretch)
Summary:
The game is cheap, if you think you might like a Bioware type RPG such as Mass Effect WITHOUT the good combat system but with an emphasis on the plot or if you like Deus Ex, get this game, beat it a few times, and join me in anticipation for the sequel at this website here.

Very solid, fast paced, and intense real time strategy game. This RTS is demanding in brain and computer power, both needing more power as the game gets bigger.
KEEP IN MIND THIS IS A MACRO RTS, MICRO IS ONLY SEEN VERY EARLY GAME.
Strategy:
Requires knowledge of the game to combat a moderately skilled player. Terrain affects troop movements, unit composition, and overall strategy.
System Editor:
Create a system of your liking and play in it with your friends or randoms. These will not be used in 1v1 competitive, only official maps will be used for those. Add asteroids, metal planets, ocean planets, even create a custom planet!
1v1 Competitive:
Challenging and intense matches take place in the 1v1 competitive scene. You probably will lose your first games due to the experienced players in ladder. To get better, watch replays of advanced players. See how they play, I watched a few and started winning instantly. Many buildings/units are not used in 1v1 because many of them are for very long games with huge systems.
Custom:
This is where the interplanetary battling takes place. Create huge systems and go to battle against your enemies systems away. Most of the units not used in 1v1 are used here. Most fun with huge battles with friends.
There are many units and strategies to use and infinite possibilities. Smash planets into your foes, teleport nukes into your enemy's base, there are many game finishers to choose from.
TL;DR: Planetary Annhilation Titans is a fun, fast paced RTS that challenges new players and provides intense battles that span the solar system. Worth it, especially with friends.

For me, this is one of the very few Yuri Visual Novels, and was a must-buy from what I heard. And I have no regrets- it is definitely worth the price-tag as well. Most will scoff at it, but this is very long for a Visual Novel- you have the main story scenes, the side-story scenes(marked by cherries on the planner), and then you also get access to post-main-story scenes which are represented by apples in the planner and are unlocked by making different choices in the main story. I did not expect to get character interaction between certain characters(namely those outside couples), but the apple extra stories have become some of my favorites since those characters that may have not gotten much love in the main and side stories shine here. This Visual Novel is huge, simply put. In terms of time, I have put in roughly 27 hours so far and have not finished all the extra scenes yet.
The bottom line- if you like Visual Novels at all, this is pretty much a must-buy.

I bought Yurirei for the #yuritopia, but, surprisingly, that no longer feels adequate. No......not at all.
Granted, #yuritopia is definitely an apt, one-word description for this VN, but....well....it's too substantial. Of course, Liar-soft knows their target audience quite well, so it is ultimately, uh, quite scandalous. So, it is obviously not nearly as philosophical as Utena or as strict as Hourou Musuko or as dramatic as Maria-sama. It's not that deep. But, it's not as fluffy as Yuruyuri or Love Live either. If I had to place it, I suppose it's spiritually not far off from Aoi Hana or maybe, Sasameki Koto?
I think Yurirei is smarter than both of those though.
To begin with, Yuna is neither ditzy nor particularly shy. Her mature, reliable personality is the freshest possible gasp of autumn air as a female protagonist. Her quiet confidence is intoxicating, her mannerisms are delightful, and I identify with the way she thinks immensely. She does have some of the cold and withdrawn characteristics that I see more often in male protagonists, such as the famous Tomoya Okazaki, but she is about twice as caring, 10 times smarter, and 100 times as responsible as that guy. Hina is also amazing, even more so as seen through Yuna's eyes. Her blunt cuteness is not some ____dere gimmick, but the main pillar of her personality, and she is, in many ways, just as responsible and intelligent as Yuna herself.
In fact, in general, these writers seem to revel in introducing certain tropes, then annihilating them. In a low quality story, Aki would really just be an uptight prude that gets "broken in" by Youka. Then, their relationship would have no meaning beyond 'opposites attract.' Seina would just be a shy freshman. Tsukuyo would really be an incompetent teacher. Nena would just be a dumb girl that falls asleep all the time. In most stories of this type, I tend to think to myself, "How are these people so thick and clueless?" In Yurirei, I am just as likely to think, "Oh, I didn't realize she'd already thought about it that much." or "Whoa, that was quite perceptive."
Ah, I fear I may have already spoiled too much. For maximum enjoyment, please go in blind now.
*ahem*
The focus is on characterization, not panties; this is a story of romance, not sex: the uncertain confession, the embarassed atmosphere, the soft touch on the arm, tension, suspense, and ectasy. Their relationships develop in a way that feels natural, despite the manipulation by Yuna and our resident ghosts. Couples respect each others' boundaries, and they care deeply for each other. They plan their future together. They talk about how their parents or society might perceive them. Unnecessary fanservice is minimal, and even when kinky stuff finally starts happening, the art doesn't zoom in on their boobs, but does a great job of showing their expressions and body language; it is all rather sensual, and, imo, in very very good taste.
Hence, in case you haven't figured it out yet, if you're buying this just to, uh, yuri your yuri, you're probably going to be extremely disappointed.
However, if you're a true yuri lover like me (hehe), you will fall in love with this......as I have.

After a LOOONG wait, it's finally out of Early Access. And it's a success.
It finally has an actual story, which is sort of good, could be better, but good.
The amount of races is pretty nice (6 races with story relevance, 7 total), ranging from your average, run-of-the-mill spacefaring humans to plant people and the aforementioned Novakids, which are essentially sentient stars.
All races are statistically the same, only difference being their looks and interactions with other characters.
The combat system is simple, but has a surprising amount of depth to it (like Terraria/Minecraft, but removes on-contact damage if you hit an enemy, also includes dual-wielding for 1-handed weapons and special attacks for 2-handed ones)
Second to last thing I'll mention is the near-limitless supply of worlds to explore. There's a good bit of variety on planet generation, ranging from your average, grassy, calm world to an absolute fireball of a planet with nothing but lava and robot castles of pure, hard steel.
For the hard-working and perfectionist builders out there, Starbound's got ya covered with "lifeless" planets, where the only thing there is you, your tools, and the canvas that is the planet itself.
Finally, at last, the boss battles and the lore.
The bosses are mostly unique, every one of them has a low chance to drop their signature weapon, and they feel simple yet fun to fight, with most having actual relevance to either the story itself, one of the races' backstories, or even both.
Speaking of lore, there's quite a lot of lore surrounding each race (save for one, but they're most likely going to be fleshed out in the near future), ranging from funny little codex entries to engaging, interesting stuff.
TL;DR All things considered, Starbound's a great game and you should get it if you'd like a 2D adventure game with building elements, an interesting story and lore, and an all-you-can-choose posse of playable races.

Diamo XL is an amazing creation by Nickervision Studios that has kept me enticed for the short period of time that I have owned it, and I presume that it will continue to do so for many more hours to come.
Essentially, Diamo XL is a game in which you try to create the outline of a diamond, moving your ball along the path from line to line. Once you have traced all the outlines you will get more points which are, points. No description needed because I assume that everyone knows what a point is. After you have been moving for a bit, you’ll notice the amount of points you get exponentially increases. This is dependant on the multiplier. You earn a higher multiplier by constantly moving around the diamond and staying alive.
There are achievements, and I speculate the developers will soon add Trading Cards to the game as they did with Orbt.XL and BitBlaster.XL. Either way, the game is very enjoyable. When you hear the words “arcade’style” or “simplistic” you might think of a boring 2d shooter game just like all the other ones out there. But Diamo XL is so much more than “the other games.” It provides a ton of fun, encourages short gaming sessions yet many of those short gaming sessions [to me. It might be different for you.] and the achievements are difficult to get, meaning that you will spend a decent amount of time before you have achieved everything.
The gameplay reminds me of something from a retro arcade in the 1990’s. Something that just keeps you entertained no matter how many times you play. It’s not like a campaign game that will fade in interest over time, it’s something that you will continue to click on months, maybe even years, from now when you’re looking for something to do.
Video review and gameplay coming soon on my youtube channel, which you can find on my profile in the “videos section”. If you’re unsure about purchasing the game, make sure you check them out when I have the time for editing!

From the creator of bit blaster XL comes another game with a similar feel, but another
style of gameplay. While bit blaster focused on shooters of yester-year in the arcades,
this focuses on a more original idea.  You are drawing lines to form a diamond while dodging enemies and raising your score. The game still feels like an arcade machine as you try
and get a high score by drawing a pattern and destroying enemies. At first it seems too
simple as you move around and collect points. But as you keep playing and getting your
score higher and keep your multiplier up you get sucked in. Enemies also evolve a bit and
destroy certain paths and block cross roads(temporaraly). Keeping your speed up without
dying is challenging and addicting.
The graphics and sound are minimalistic and don't draw you in, but this isn't a bad thing
as I felt it allowed you to focus on the gameplay. The controls are fine, any mistake you make will be your fault as things get chaotic and you make a mistake in a panic. There are unlockable characters with different stats and sizes to vary things up a bit, though this does bring me to my one critsism. Unlocking characters are cool but the gameplay really could use more stages (or patterens so to speak). There is only one and yes this game is cheap, but thats how much I enjoyed it. Having more would be really sweet and give the game more meat. But again this game is cheap so i'm not gonna criticize this too much. But I do hope the developer expands on this game. It was a nice suprise and like "bit blaster" it's fun, addictive, and nails the feel of being back in the arcades of the 90's.

Ok now, on to the review of this game.
Diamo XL is a very simple game. That's not a bad thing. That's actually a GOOD thing.
In this game, you move a square around a diamond with two intersecting lines going through the middle to form four right triangles. Once you start moving from a point, you cannot stop until you get to the next point. The only thing you can do is slow down by letting go of whatever button you're using to move or speed up by holding it down. Red shapes will come from the sides of the screen and go towards the diamond shape that you can move on. As you may have guessed, these are enemies and touching one will kill you. When you move across a line, it turns blue. If you turn all of the lines blue, you get a relatively large score bonus. Running into small blue circles will also give you points. You can earn a score multiplier of up to 5x by constantly being in motion. Stopping for more than about a second will cause your score multyiplier to quickly go down.
That's everything I can think of on how to play. That's it. Just a few sentences. A medium-sized paragraph sums up the entiree game.
But trust me. The game's fun. Simple isn't bad. In Pac-Man, you moved a yellow circle around a maze and got small white dots. That game is still played today.
Recommended, strongly recommended, and that's all I have to say.

I didn't really expect that the game was going to be as amazing as most people probably wanted it to be, I really just wanted a Fallout game on an engine updated to at least Skyrim's standards.
Some of the new features of the Fallout 4 version of the engine I can't live without anymore, like the Rain occlusion. I couldn't stand seeing rain fall through roofs in Skyrim (thank Todd for Special Edition, amirite?).
That being said, I hope for future games they can move to another engine that doesn't have the awful quirks that the Gamebryo/Creation engine has. (i.e. physics freaking out when fps is over 60).

This is Christopher Nolan's 'Interstellar' all over again - I can't tell whether I love it, hate it or just don't care.
It's quite the depature from FO3 in terms of having the overall tone and RPG elements exchanged for far tighter combat and gameplay. You only have to walk a few feet in any direction to find a mission or 'scenario' unfolding and while this makes it far more accessible and satisfying in the short term, I never really felt like I was undertaking a real 'role in the universe'.
In FO4, I feel like I'm not discovering hidden treasures in a wasteland so much as picking through treasures that were specifically put there for me to find. That said, I do find the characters, gameplay, crafting, building and missions themselves highly, highly entertaining and a significant, allbeit iterative improvement on FO3.
If this game had the ambition, cohesion and narrative diversity of New Vegas, it'd be the greatest in the series by a long shot. As it happens, I think it's a solid but small step forward for the franchise and while I love it when all the elements come together, I can't help but feel there's a massive missed opportunity when viewing the game as the sum of its parts.

Bastion sets a high standard for all other indie games.  I purchased it over a year ago and finally decided to write a review on it because it is one of my favorite games of all time and I just started playing Transistor, Supergiant's second title.
Combat: 8/10
The combat is fluid and enjoyable, and it feels unique despite the inherent similarity it has to other action RPGs.  However, it is not without its flaws.  It is possible in many situations to exploit certain weapons (esp. the mortar) to avoid fights entirely.  Additionally, the enemies lack a lot of variety.  Despite these shortcomings the combat is very involved and the controls are tight.  Never do you die in this game without knowing exactly what you did wrong.
Soundtrack: 10/10
Bastion simply has the best soundtrack I've ever heard in a game.  Darren Korb does not phone it in on any tracks.  It is one of the few soundtracks I still come back to for recreational listening.  The soundtrack plays a large part in making Bastion greatly immersive.
Environment: 9/10
As I mentioned above, Bastion is very immersive.  The environments are beautiful and the art style is very easy on the eyes.  Not much to say other than its serves as a good example of how art can function in games and the game itself can become a piece of art to look upon.
Story: 9/10
Supergiant, as I have discovered from Transistor, has a certain way of telling stories in games.  Very few characters actually speak in game which adds a degree of mystery to the plot/lore and allows for the gamer to fill in the blanks.  I support this choice.  It keeps the quality of the voice cast high while not taking away from the story.  The immediate story is right in front of you the entire time and there is a relatively clear end goal.  The complete story, however, is told through the descriptions of items, the side comments and observations made by the narrator, the soundtrack, and the actions of NPCs.  It is rare in game plots to find much ambiguity but Bastion does a wonderful job of crafting a world in which that ambiguity allowed me to create a vast world in my imagination.
Additional Features/Things I Didn't Want to Put in Other Categories: 7/10
This is where the game has some of its greatest shortcomings but there are some very bright spots still.  I'll start with the bad.  The "Memorial" operates as a sort of challenge board, which is a nice idea, but I don't think it was very well implemented.  It just seemed tacked on as an extra upgrade to the Bastion that was needed.  Additionally, many of the weapons are just not that good.  Not what you start with either.  Some weapons acquired halfway through the game are noticeably less powerful than the starting ones.  However, all of the weapons feel unique so that's a definite plus and perhaps there was some strategy to them that I missed.
On to the Bastion.  Being able to upgrade the Bastion in whatever order you want is a nice touch and I really enjoyed being able to get the features I wanted when I wanted them.  It added additional satisfaction to advancing through the game because I got to find out just what that new upgrade was!  The leveling system was interesting and I'm not going to go too in-depth because this review is becoming a novel but it allows you to choose potions with given effects (some good and some bad) each level.  You can respec whenever.
Now my favorite unique part of the Bastion.  The Idol system.  Idols are the statues of the old gods of the world that the player acquires by advancing through the game.  Each Idol confers an experience bonus to the player while buffing the enemies in some way.  This is a great way to increase the difficulty while not making it feel artificial with arbitrary health and damage buffs to enemies that make the game impossible.  They just make the game more fun because its more challenging.
I think that sums up my review nicely and is a pretty succinct way to show why I enjoy the game so much.  Aside from the excellent story, soundtrack, and visual environment, Bastion is simply fun because it is challenging.  That's good for a game.  That's how a game should be.

This game is very similar to earlier versions of Runescape though for some reason a lot of the players don't like the comparison.  It is very simple but surprisingly addicting.  The world isn't that large, but it's large enough to keep you busy for awhile.  They have plenty of mobs to keep things interesting.  The combat is very easy, it's really hard to die if you pay attention (the mobs don't move and you can move away after 3 hits if you need to).  The community is very helpful, but as it grows you begin to get a few jerks that leak in and the larger it gets the more of these you have to deal with.  The moderators do a good job of dealing with them for the most part though.  The worse thing about the game is probably the excessive censorship.  They have a chat channel on just about every topic you can think of and you get in "trouble" if you start talking off-topic in a channel.  The main problem is that there is only one channel that ever has much of a population on it (the default channel).    The best part of the game is it's free!  They have opportunities to use real money to help yourself in the game (or just help the developer(s)), but they really aren't that necessary.  It surprises me how often people spend money on a free game, a bit of an oxymoron, but it's there.  That's fine, it's their money and they can do with it as they wish, just doesn't make a lot of sense to me.
Overall, the game is somewhat fun for awhile though it starts to get boring after a bit.  It's a grinder so it can be repetitious, a little addictive and boring after awhile.  The price point on the game can't be beaten so if you liked early Runescape you don't have anything to lose (other than a little time) in giving RPG MO a GO!

This game was just...wow.
I put about 16 hours into my first playthrough of this game, but you could get through the campaign in probably just one or two. An hour or two of my playtime I was AFK, but the rest of it? How did I get so much more time out of it?
Reading.
Yup, you read that right. I spent a dozen hours just reading in this game, and I don't think I even found everything there was to read. You see, this entire game takes place on a single ship, asking questions about a single murder, and yet, somehow, this team has put together the foundation for an entire universe inside of this tiny little game. Instead of exploring a massive world, doing quests and collecting bits and pieces of lore along the way, it's all laid out for you in a computer database filled with journals, clips from newspapers, transcripts of audio files, blogs, and pretty much any form of medium you can think of.
Each story is broken up into pieces, some having all of the pieces lined up nicely for you, others you have to go digging for. When I first got into the database, the sheer amount of information seemed daunting, but the more I read, the more I got sucked into this world. It shows you how this universe came to be the way it did, noting several historical events that changed the course of their history from ours (such as Italy siding with the Central Powers during WWI and Hitler's assassination in the beginning of WWII).
Without getting into spoilers, it also hints at some potentially darker aspects of everything that's going on. There seem to be mysteries within mysteries, and every answer you find just gives you more questions to wonder about.
Before I end this, just a couple of things I noticed that could be improved upon:
1) There were a number of spelling mistakes within the database as well as some of the subtitles not quite matching with the dialogue. Some of the spelling mistakes seem to be intentional (like putting those mysterious "21"s around everywhere) while others seem to be actual mistakes (using bear instead of bare, simple misspellings, etc). While they *do* slightly take away from the immersion of the game, they definitely don't break it. And the misprints with the dialogue still tell the same idea, it just isn't always the exact same phrasing.
2) This is really just a minor annoyance, but it's kind of annoying that you can see the "+/-" symbol for the dropdown menu of crew relations on your main HUD but you can only access it when you're on the inventory or main menu screen. Either don't make it visible on the HUD or let us access it directly through a shortkut key (like, say, the "+" or "-" key).
3) Speaking of crew relations, I would absolutely love more opportunities to interact with the crew. The depth they've created for their world is amazing, but apart from a couple of main characters, the rest of the crew seems kind of bland, just given a quirk to run with. The Induction Summary Interviews are nice, but it'd be nice to actually see their backgrounds play out through our interaction with them. Looking at the sequel, it seems like there won't be much interaction with the crew apart from over the CMC, so I guess they were more concerned with world-building than relationships, which I get. Although if I'm being really honest with myself, I just wanted more of a chance to flirt with Carla. She was the first person I met outside of my cabin and I guess I couldn't help but want to get to know more about her.
4) Last (and definitely the least) of my issues with this game is the graphics. You can tell they're a bit dates. But you know what? It doesn't take away from the story, it doesn't make combat any more difficult, and so ultimately, it doesn't take away from the game. I'm really just putting this hear to let you know that it's there. This isn't the prettiest game out there, but it's what's on the inside that counts, right?
Now if you'll excuse me, I'm ready to jump back into this thing so that I can try to figure out...well, everything.

If you like yuri or VN you may want to support this game for the future of the genre.
First of all, I have played the Japanese version a few years back. The game is fantastic. Probably one of the best takes in VN form on the yuri genre. It's light hearted, often funny and very touching towards the end, "healing", and characters are very cute. The things you may criticize in this game are mostly attributable to the development budget. That said, I can't comment on the translation. I assume it will be fine enough. The original text is plain and simple and I assume it remains as readable translated.
Liar soft is one of the VN companies with a more indie feel. It makes very unique and fun games, though not necessarily with the highest production value. You can say it occupies a niche spot in an already niche market.
Often times this is reflected in the fact that there is limited voice acting. That just means mostly the writer was more ambitious than the budget allowed in terms of full voice acting. I would also point out that although the consensus is fully voiced acted VNs are the way to go, partial voice acting allows writing of longer monologues, which some may enjoy.
Now I was really surprised this game got released on Steam uncensored. The price is high but it's what you would expect for a limited audience release. If you buy this game it may encourage them to make bigger budget works with western release in schedule. When the volume is higher obviously that allows for different pricing schemes.
Finally let me reiterate that the game is fantastic, espcially if you are a genre lover of yuri--it's not to be missed. If you can't get it now, wish list it and check it out later.

-No factions. Everyone gets the same units and buildings.

A pros/cons rundown and some thoughts, for those thinking of buying the game! Sorry it's a little long,,
Pros:
- Very very cute art! A good variety of sprites, expressions, and CGs.
- Catchy and effective OST, with an included “music room” to listen to all the tracks.
- Each character is distinct, has their own background, thoughts, motives, goals, personality, and problems/flaws that are all very relatable, or easy to sympathize with.
- The couples’ stories were all really compelling, and each and every one felt like it had something to offer.
- Some common yuri tropes are addressed and consulted, exposed for their flaws, or given a very human, realistic spin to them.
- While it was nothing mind-blowing, the story was always engaging in some way, and EXTREMELY emotionally investing. I cannot stress enough how invested this game gets you into its interesting and compelling cast of characters, and all their relationships with each other, romantic or otherwise. I cried and burst out laughing and smiled and was on the edge of my seat and relieved and every other emotional a game could make you feel. (well, except for afraid maybe, haha)
- SO. MUCH. EXTRA. CONTENT. AFTER THE MAIN STORY. Hours worth of extra scenes are unlocked based on what choices you pick in the game, so make sure to save at every choice so you can easily unlock them all!
- The sex scenes were all incredibly tender and sweet, with beautiful art in CGs, and none of them felt gross or overly fanservice-y. (though the lack of Super Explicit Content might be a negative for some people)
Cons/stuff to keep in mind:
- Not all the scenes have voice acting. Only major story events, couple events, and scenes that have CGs include voice acting.
- I’m not a fan of a good handful of the voices. Too many of them are shrill and high-pitched, which can be pretty annoying, especially with the characters who are also loud and cheerful on top of that. (I recently found out this might because a LOT of the voice actors are reused for multiple characters)
- Almost ALL the characters have obnoxiously high-pitched and squeaky voice acting during sex scenes.Doesn't ruin it, but it IS off-putting for me.
- The background music doesn't loop; it fades out and then restarts, which can break immersion for some people.
- No agency, and therefore no routes. The main character, Yuna, is entirely her own character, with her own goals and wishes and feelings. So, you can’t change the outcome of situations or the story. YOU the player don’t really have a say, and are only along for the ride. I know that tons of people will be disappointed to know that there are no routes and no agency on their part.
- There’s a couple that’s a teacher and a student. Their relationship lacks the manipulation and toxic power-imbalance that plagues teacher-student sort of relationships, and so I personally was able to find enjoyment in their story, but I know that others might not, so I’m putting this out there now. (note: it is possible to speed through their scenes and arc by selecting the "Skip unread text" option in the options menu and then using the skip button)
- Unlocking all the extras can be kind of confusing. Not too hard, but a bit of a pain
- Some of the sex scenes felt out of nowhere, or like they weren't properly lead up to
- The sex scenes are also WAY TOO SHORT. Could've used some more detail in the text and, like… fumbling and exploring and learning.
- Some of the dialogue in the sex scenes was so over-the-top or weirdly put that it was unintentionally funny
- And finally, there's a glitch that me and a friend of mine have, though I haven't heard of anyone else dealing with this yet. About every 15-20 minutes, the game will dramatically slow down and stop progressing, and nothing but closing will fix it. I found a way to slowly save the game and then close from the menu, but it's a bit irritating to pull off. Didn't bother me too bad, but I know it'd be a huge pain for some people. Hopefully this glitch is extremely uncommon.
And finally, some tips:
- SAVE AT EVERY CHOICE. You will need to go back to them to unlock all the extras, and they are WORTH IT.
- NEVER. FORCE CLOSE. THE. GAME. EVER. It'll insist that you haven't completed scenes that you have, and make you redo them just to move on in the story, every time you force close. Always close from the menu.
- If you live with other people, wear headphones. Trust me.
Final thoughts? This game was an absolutely joy to play, especially for its great cast of characters and compelling stories. Absolutely worth the price and more, for me, and I hope others will enjoy the game as much as I did!

Zone 4 is a classic design,arcade themed,fighting MMO that offers endless hours of fun. From pvp to pve arcades teaming up with your friends and even taking on zombies. with 8 regular classes to choose from and an additional 4 premium classes you're spoiled for choice in this outstanding world of fighters. With 6 models to choose from and an endless supply of costumes/gear you will find the game to be hilarious,ridiculous,amazing and putting a smile on your face. The fighting mechanics are quite simple yet offer a lot of depth at the same time. The controls may seem easy at first "A for dodge" "S for grab" and "D for strike" + directional keys to move your character around but there's quite a complex combo system that requires a bit of timing and commitment to be able to master and when I say combos I am talking 20+ 30+ hit combos and (although situational) even infinite combos.
The game encourages you to make some friends, team up with them and accomplish quests to obtain items to progress in the game. There's a skill upgrade system, a gear upgrade system, drilling and fishing (these are given free daily) for in game currency (ZEN) and if you're lucky you could get something of value and sell it for a big profit depending on what it is. Now there are certainly some people that have completely gotten this game wrong and I'll tell you why, there are people in this game who are of high level and have some of the best gear in the game along with some of the highest skill damage percentages and all of the bells and whistles to boot.
Now many people do make purchases in the game to buy and sell things to obtain enough zen to buy or even craft something rare or legendary and that's totally their choice but that doesn't make the game a pay 2 win system. You can very well complete your daily quests, make good use of your daily prizes (drills/rods), grind in arcades,zombie battles and pvp and save your zen for something valuable. Everybody gets a free costume at level 10 and there are plenty of timed rare costumes that are reasonably cheap that are still very much competitively accepted in PVP however you should remember that PVP is only one part of the game so don't be discouraged if you're getting beaten by a pro with amazing gear. You always have a choice if you wish to participate in a fighting room or not and to be honest the best thing to do is make friends and progress through the game together. Too many people who give bad reviews here are heavily focused on the higher level PVP arena and because they don't have what a high level pro might have automatically they've branded the game P2W and this simply isn't the case. After a LOOONG wait, it's finally out of Early Access. And it's a success.
It finally has an actual story, which is sort of good, could be better, but good.
The amount of races is pretty nice (6 races with story relevance, 7 total), ranging from your average, run-of-the-mill spacefaring humans to plant people and the aforementioned Novakids, which are essentially sentient stars.
All races are statistically the same, only difference being their looks and interactions with other characters.
The combat system is simple, but has a surprising amount of depth to it (like Terraria/Minecraft, but removes on-contact damage if you hit an enemy, also includes dual-wielding for 1-handed weapons and special attacks for 2-handed ones)
Second to last thing I'll mention is the near-limitless supply of worlds to explore. There's a good bit of variety on planet generation, ranging from your average, grassy, calm world to an absolute fireball of a planet with nothing but lava and robot castles of pure, hard steel.
For the hard-working and perfectionist builders out there, Starbound's got ya covered with "lifeless" planets, where the only thing there is you, your tools, and the canvas that is the planet itself.
Finally, at last, the boss battles and the lore.
The bosses are mostly unique, every one of them has a low chance to drop their signature weapon, and they feel simple yet fun to fight, with most having actual relevance to either the story itself, one of the races' backstories, or even both.
Speaking of lore, there's quite a lot of lore surrounding each race (save for one, but they're most likely going to be fleshed out in the near future), ranging from funny little codex entries to engaging, interesting stuff.
TL;DR All things considered, Starbound's a great game and you should get it if you'd like a 2D adventure game with building elements, an interesting story and lore, and an all-you-can-choose posse of playable races.

Like all of Nickervision's games, Diamo XL is a fantastic and addictive time waster.
In this game, you attempt to traverse the lines between the points of a diamond and its constituent triangles, while dodging projectiles which destroy you on contact. You gain points for covering every line that makes up the diamond, near misses, and touching dots which also randomly appear and move along said lines.
The challenge comes from the progressively more varied and numerous projectiles, some of which can even destroy lines. The longer you last, the higher your multiplier, and the faster you move (or so it seems,) the higher your score.
It's an incredibly easy to learn yet difficult to master game, equal parts imminently casual, and maddeningly challenging as you go on. You can unlock different player icons by achieving specific objectives, much like Orbt XL.
My sole criticism of the game is that movement in the desired direction seems to be most easily achieved by using up, down, left, and right, despite four of the lines being diagonal. Moreover, since (on a controller at least,) those directions are most precisely hit using the D-pad versus the analog stick, I do at times find that the direction I press is not the direction I move in, frequently leading to premature failures. This is a minor criticism however, since a) it could simply be my D-Pad, and b) keyboard controls are also available.
All in all, fun, affordable game.

Being someone who has invested over 560 hours into this game I have come to a conclusion and I want to leave my opinion on the game. These will look over various points.
1.Main Questline:
Now, I am fully aware of the get quest,kill things, get thing, get reward cycle, but in my opinion, the Main Questline is a ton of fun to play. It allows for a sense of relief and the ending is so climactic ending with a bang. However, the main story is incredibly lackluster, doesn't have many twists and I believe that some of the side quests are more memorable. There are only two quests that sparked my attention when playing the main questline: Unlikely Valentine and The Nuclear Option/Nuclear Family. This is because the climactic ending of The Nuclear Option/Nuclear Family is amazing but could have more work and Unlikely Valentine has the most interesting character introduced (Detective Nick Valentine). All the other quests didn't really give me any reason to remember them.
2.Side Quests:
The side quests in this game are awesome. Be it helping a rocket powered ship take off or finding a delusional man with a strange alien artifact the games side quests are great. However the side quests that really stood out to me are: The Last Voyage of The USS Constitution, The Cabot Family Questline, The Silver Shroud, Detective Case Files and Pickman's gallery Quest. These are all incredibly unique to the fallout franchise. Where else are you going to pretend you are a superhero with a silver tommy gun and kill drug dealers?
3.Replayability:
With 566 hours clogged into this game, I have many, many different characters, all different builds, all unique. The game allows great customisability with your characters. Be it a stelathy ninja, a knight in power armour or a sadistic lunatic who eats people, you can be who you wanna be. The game offers tons and tons of random encounters. meaning the place you go to will always be different. You can play this game for hours on end.
4.Factions:
Terrible. You either be a xenophobic self-rightous gang, a freedom fighting xenophobic gang, scientist slavers or a group of civillians who can't shut up about settlements. 2 are the same, 1 is evil and 1 always needs your help. Take your pick.
5.Companions:
Terrible again. Apart from nick valentine, dogmeat or the robots you can make in automatron. I don't use any of the other companions, maybe cait but that's it. The affinity system is good but can be annoying, frustrating and downright horrid at times.
6.Settlement System:
Not bad. But, it doesn't just work. Settlers don't assign, There is a space LIMIT, and some settlers can't be moved.
7. Creation Club:
You know I had to mention this. First off, You don't have to use the creation club or pay for it. Second, It isn't paid mods, it is a buisness practice to make addons and pay mod makers the money they rightfully deserve. Lastly, again you don't HAVE to use it, it is just an option.
8.Mods:
Speaks for itself really.
9.Overall:
If anyone wants a great post-apocalyptic first person shooter. Then Fallout 4 may not be perfect but is a damn good example of how fun games can be. 6.5/10

Bastion sets a high standard for all other indie games.  I purchased it over a year ago and finally decided to write a review on it because it is one of my favorite games of all time and I just started playing Transistor, Supergiant's second title.
Combat: 8/10
The combat is fluid and enjoyable, and it feels unique despite the inherent similarity it has to other action RPGs.  However, it is not without its flaws.  It is possible in many situations to exploit certain weapons (esp. the mortar) to avoid fights entirely.  Additionally, the enemies lack a lot of variety.  Despite these shortcomings the combat is very involved and the controls are tight.  Never do you die in this game without knowing exactly what you did wrong.
Soundtrack: 10/10
Bastion simply has the best soundtrack I've ever heard in a game.  Darren Korb does not phone it in on any tracks.  It is one of the few soundtracks I still come back to for recreational listening.  The soundtrack plays a large part in making Bastion greatly immersive.
Environment: 9/10
As I mentioned above, Bastion is very immersive.  The environments are beautiful and the art style is very easy on the eyes.  Not much to say other than its serves as a good example of how art can function in games and the game itself can become a piece of art to look upon.
Story: 9/10
Supergiant, as I have discovered from Transistor, has a certain way of telling stories in games.  Very few characters actually speak in game which adds a degree of mystery to the plot/lore and allows for the gamer to fill in the blanks.  I support this choice.  It keeps the quality of the voice cast high while not taking away from the story.  The immediate story is right in front of you the entire time and there is a relatively clear end goal.  The complete story, however, is told through the descriptions of items, the side comments and observations made by the narrator, the soundtrack, and the actions of NPCs.  It is rare in game plots to find much ambiguity but Bastion does a wonderful job of crafting a world in which that ambiguity allowed me to create a vast world in my imagination.
Additional Features/Things I Didn't Want to Put in Other Categories: 7/10
This is where the game has some of its greatest shortcomings but there are some very bright spots still.  I'll start with the bad.  The "Memorial" operates as a sort of challenge board, which is a nice idea, but I don't think it was very well implemented.  It just seemed tacked on as an extra upgrade to the Bastion that was needed.  Additionally, many of the weapons are just not that good.  Not what you start with either.  Some weapons acquired halfway through the game are noticeably less powerful than the starting ones.  However, all of the weapons feel unique so that's a definite plus and perhaps there was some strategy to them that I missed.
On to the Bastion.  Being able to upgrade the Bastion in whatever order you want is a nice touch and I really enjoyed being able to get the features I wanted when I wanted them.  It added additional satisfaction to advancing through the game because I got to find out just what that new upgrade was!  The leveling system was interesting and I'm not going to go too in-depth because this review is becoming a novel but it allows you to choose potions with given effects (some good and some bad) each level.  You can respec whenever.
Now my favorite unique part of the Bastion.  The Idol system.  Idols are the statues of the old gods of the world that the player acquires by advancing through the game.  Each Idol confers an experience bonus to the player while buffing the enemies in some way.  This is a great way to increase the difficulty while not making it feel artificial with arbitrary health and damage buffs to enemies that make the game impossible.  They just make the game more fun because its more challenging.
I think that sums up my review nicely and is a pretty succinct way to show why I enjoy the game so much.  Aside from the excellent story, soundtrack, and visual environment, Bastion is simply fun because it is challenging.  That's good for a game.  That's how a game should be.

This will be my first review so bear with me and to avoid spoilers I will mention no names or events from in game.
All in all, this game has been so much fun (I'd have preferred an all ages version instead but hey whatever, beggars cant be choosers).
Before I start with the good though I thought it might be easier to list the problems with it, because sadly its not perfect.
1. The Voice Acting (VA) - For the most part the casting was spot on, the majority of characters fit well with their VA's however there were at least two cases were the VA's were horribly miss cast. They absolutely don't fit their respective characters. One especially more glaring than the other, and if you've watched as many anime and played as many VN as I have this can be  quite a major sore point.
2. R+18 bits - Considering the premise it had to be done, otherwise the kindred spirits (or yuri-re as they want to be called) wouldn't be able to pass on. That said I believe that the game has massive potential to be a all ages love story that transcends gender boundaries. Simple and sweet. So I genuinely believe its R+18 portions actually hold it back.
And with that over lets move on to the pros.
Story - It's simple, it really is, there is no great drama, no dark mystery, no epic adventure, no grand revenge quest, nothing of that sort. But it works well for pieces like this. As an avid player of visual novels (VN) I've seen quite a myriad genres so, sometimes a nice fun and simple story like this is really just the best. 9/10
Art - As with the story its fairly simple but well drawn, the art is crisp and nice, the character design was well thought out, each character having their own distincts faces and quirks. It's nothing impressive but theres nothing to complain about either. 8/10
Music/BGM - Same with the story it is failry simple, however they fit the mood of each respective story arc really well. Nothing on the level of Two Steps from Hell but then again this isn't that type of game. 8/10
Characters - Easily the best part of the game, I love the characters, ALL of THEM, they've all got their own personalities and quirks as well as distinct visual differences. Can't say much about them without bringing in spoilers but the attention to detail to each one is very pleasing espeically since they have a large cast of characters. And the character design is also well done, each individual is distinct from the other. This is actually impressive as even some highly praised VN's out there fall victim to their characters essentially being hair or skin color swapped versions of each other. 10/10
Gameplay - The format this VN uses is actually quite uniqe and refreshing and it also gets rid of the annoying repetitve nature of most other VN's when your chasing diffrent character arcs. It however means that replayability will sadly be non-existent save for reminesence. So it remains to be seen wether this is a good or bad idea. 8/10
Enjoyment - I love Yuri VN's and its a damn shame more aren't in the english market. This was a nice change of pace however so it comes highly recomended. 10/10
Overall - The Pros heavily , HEAVILY, outwiegh the cons so... 8.83/10
TL;DR: I highly recommend this game to anyone who isn't averse to the genre (VN's or Yuri). And to those who are you, may want to try it anyway, they do have moments where it makes you think twice about the issues whichare often associated with same sex relationships.

So... It is really hard to review this game right now, as it is. It's fun. It's good. It's Street Fighter, one of the better fighting games out there, but the thing about this game right now is:
It has definitly been released too early. For the people who played Super or Ultra Street Fighter IV it'll be a really weird experience, since this game hasn't been polished even remotely as much as the later versions of Street Fighter IV.
I'll put some of the more weird things right here.
1.  It has no PS3 Controller Support (Many people have PS3 Arcade Sticks, such as me, so you're forced to use external software to use them)
2. They're slowly adding new characters which you need to purchase, not through real money, but this ingame currency you earn by playing.
3. There is close to no singleplayer content. The stories, compared to Street Fighter IV are incredibly short, 3-4 fights usually and the stories themselves are really not good at all. You might say the Story was never too good, but it is still not much at all.
You're still able to play this game and I personally enjoy it alot, but as it is right now, it should be tagged an "Early Access Game"
So do not buy this game if you expect a game as polished as Super or Ultra Street Fighter IV. Do buy this game, if you wanna watch this game grow, because it'll grow over time.
On a side note: They got rid of "Games for Windows Live" which made online a billion times better. It still has lags, which is really annoying when playing online, but it's either your PC / connection or your opponents.
Overall this game has the potential to be an incredibly good Street Fighter game, but right now it is not enough.
I still do recommend the game, since I am still enjoying playing it (alot) and even though lag is infuriating, even though Ken looks weird, Cammy looks like her face is made out of porcelain and even though there's not alot of content in single player, outside of survival, the game is still fun and I'll rake up a ton of gameplay time in it, which in the end is all that counts. Me (or you) enjoying my/yourself while playing this game, which I do.

Bonjour,
Je vais vous faire une évaluation en deux parties, la première concernera le background du jeu et la seconde le gameplay, ce à quoi on a accès pour l'instant et mon impression.
TLDR : je recommande le jeu pour ceux qui souhaiteraient participer au financement ou aux curieux. L'intérêt de ce jeu, c'est son histoire, et pour le moment, seul le prologue est disponible aux joueurs, le reste du jeu est plus ou moins un survival d'exploration actuellement, mais l'histoire sera complète pour la version finale.
Alors nous y voilà. Nous sommes en 1964, en Angleterre dans la ville rétro futuriste de Wellington Wells, qui a été rebâtie pour cacher les séquelles de la Seconde Guerre mondiale.
Nous incarnons Arthur Hastings, censeur pour le journal public, car tout ce qui est lié à la guerre doit être effacé de la mémoire de la ville. Dans ce but-là, une drogue que l'on appelle Joy est distribuée aux habitants qui doivent tous la prendre régulièrement pour vivre dans le bonheur. Ceux qui oublient de la prendre y sont rappelés puis forcés, mais ceux qui refusent de la prendre sont renvoyés dans les quartiers pauvres marqués par la guerre, où tout le monde essaye de survivre.
Retournons à notre personnage, au cours de notre travail, un article à censurer nous rappel des évènements tragiques, on panique, et on est face à un dilemme, prendre notre Joy et toute notre routine continue dans le meilleur des mondes (=> crédits, fin du jeu). Ou faire face à nos souvenirs et jeter cette ♥♥♥♥♥ rose.
Je ne vais pas vous spoil le prologue, qui même s'il est court est intéressant, mais en gros, on se fait griller et on a des problèmes.
L'aventure commence alors dans un petit abri sous-terrain.
Pour ce qui est du gameplay, on est dans un survival d'infiltration, notre personnage doit faire face à ses besoins primaires (manger, boire, dormir, se soigner) tout en se fondant parmi les différents types de populations des différents quartiers.
Pour ça, on peut récolter des objets, en fabriquer, réaliser des quêtes (qui sont disponibles actuellement). Mais il faut faire attention, chacune de vos actions est observée par les pnj, qui peuvent se méfier de vous ou se sentir agressés et vous sautez à la gueule. La meilleure solution selon moi, c'est de fuir et s'excuser auprès des pnj quand la tension baisse ou revenir plus tard quand vos poursuivants lâchent l'affaire.
On peut aussi se battre, le système est plutôt basique, on peut frapper (plus ou moins fort selon notre dosage), jeter des objets (qui peuvent aussi servir de diversion), pousser, se protéger. Les coups des pnj ne pardonnent pas et les armes ont une durabilité assez courte comme votre endurance d'ailleurs (ne pas oublier que l'on est un junkie qui bossait dans un bureau toute la journée).
Pour ce qui est du craft, c'est aussi simple, les recettes se débloquent soit en ramassant les plans, soit automatiquement quand tout les objets d'une recette sont dans notre inventaire. Pour certaines recettes des établis seront nécessaires, des établis de mécanique ou de chimie, que vous trouverez soit dans certaines maisons, soit dans vos planques.
Pour les abris, vous pourrez dormir des maisons, mais si on vous choper dans une maison habitée, on ne manquera pas de vous chasser.
Pour le stockage des objets, vous pouvez prendre et déposer des objets dans chaque conteneur que vous fouillez, mais gardez à l'esprit que les seuls conteneurs qui ne sont pas reset quand vous traversez un pont vers un autre quartier sont ceux de vos abris.
Mes impressions sur le jeu sont plutôt positives. On est sur de l'accès anticipé et malgré le manque d'histoire principale les mécaniques du jeu sont là, le cycle jour/nuit et peut-être trop bref actuellement.
J'attends l'histoire principale du jeu, la transition un peu brève entre le prologue et l'abri m'a un peu déçu, mais il me semble qu'il y a une intervention d'un autre personnage de l'histoire, qui n'est pas inclue dans la version actuelle.
Je modifierai mon évaluation en fonction des ajouts majeurs.
Pour conclure, dans son stade actuel, je recommande le jeu pour les curieux ou ceux qui souhaiteraient participer au financement. En effet, nous sommes sur de l'early acces, de l'avant-première quoi, la demande devait être importante ce qui justifie l'absence d'histoire.
Pour le prix, même chose qu'au-dessus, certes pour certains, c'est cher pour le contenu actuel, mais on est sur de l'early acces. Ce serait une perte pour le studio de brader le jeu alors qu'ils sont encore en plein développement. Selon moi, le prix est juste, peut-être qu'il va baisser quand la version finale sera disponible.
Pour les joueurs recherchant un jeu complet, soyez patients, ce jeu n'est pas encore pour vous. À la limite essayez-le avec le remboursement Steam, mais je doute que vous trouviez le jeu assez intéressant sans l'histoire.

I have loved this game for a very long time, i have a great passion for puzzle games and this game was included in my childhood. This game honestly fills my head with nostalgia every single time i play it, there are so many pro's to this game that its hard to list them all!
But no game is without flaws, and Puzzle Pirates has some flaws that a lot of people cant seem to look past, this unfortunately makes it so that the player count is very low... but more on that later.
Pro:-
There its a lot to do on puzzle pirates in general, its your classic open world "Do what you want" type of game, based in a 2.5D world where you can create and customise your pirate however you want them to look, You start out with your own little shack on a random island as far as i'm aware, honestly i never looked into it.
All of the puzzles in this game all have different layouts, gameplay strategies and ways to win (understandable, otherwise it wouldnt be a good puzzle game would it?)
Wide ocean full of bots and players to explore and pillage with, the option (when you get the money ofcourse) and the option to take any station you like, given you are on a bot boat. If you manage to find a player driven boat, you may be told to take any station, or assigned your own.
Create your own fierce pirate clan, or join others, band together to take over the seas. honestly it's the best part of the game, owning your own boat and sailing across the ocean to fight bots and players.
Con's
As i've said multiple time, there is one major flaw right now on PP, and that is the amount of active players... Unfortunately like every game, MMO's to be exact really, the player base is bound to decline at some point, and puzzle pirates has been active a very long time. Its a shame to see one of my favourite old games become empty and void, and it really does take the fun out of it now since the bot's in the ocean's are mostly incredibly difficult to deal with alone, without a player based crew, it is very unlikely you would pass many pillages without being hit badly by overpowered bots.
Conclusion
To summerise really, its a fantastic game, but the player base is now incredibly low. I miss the old times of pillaging around, but like all good MMO's, their time passes and without the players keeping the servers full, it takes the fun out. If the game ever picks up again, i would gladly play it again. But for now, my old War Brig sits in port. Waiting to be sailed once more by me and a vast crew of active players.
-Adyaxe, Meridian Ocean, 11 Year Veteran.

I'm not a big RTS player, but this really grabbed me. The graphics, beautiful. Everything had the massive sense of scale that a game played on a galactic scale needs, and yet still had enough detail in each of the units for me to just spend five or so minutes staring at my units, admiring how nice they look.
