The game ran AMAZINGLY, supporting hundreds of units on screen at any given time, even when I had a second picture in picture screen displaying some of the busiest regions of the game. I almost never experienced lag, and when I did, it was generally because of a background task on my computer. As for the gameplay, as I said I'm not a big RTS player so I can't really compare it to much, but what I have played is thoroughly entertaining - addictive even. Since I spent about 4 hours straight playing matches of the game over and over, I reckon you could say I liked it. All in all, definitely worth the $31 US it costs, but if you're not willing to spend that much, wait for it to go on sale, and buy it. Either way, buy this game, because it's all round fantastic.

Starbound is a 2D survival platfomer where you caan go from planet to planet, Sounds like they took terraria and just put it into space right? wrong, I don't really find one better than the other, but starbound is alot different than terraria.the 2D sanbox survival part, might actually be the only similarity.
Pros:
Has really good character customization, where you can pick from multiple different races, which race you pick doesn't really effect gameplay without mods.
Has a really good intro that shows you how to use the controlls.(If you choose not to skip it that is)
The game looks great, I love the pixel art, I do have a slight problem with the character heads, but i used a mod to fix that. theres also good cutscenes that don't have voices but are still pretty good.
The colonies are really cool, you can have people that live in your town, that have missions for you and also pat rent. you can even make these towns people into crew members if you do enough missions for them.
The missions and bosses are also pretty cool, and can ceep you busy, even when you're pretty overpowered, they are easy though if you are OP.
The planets have a pretty good difficulty curve, making the planets with better materials, harder to survive.,(especially visible in Frackin Universe)
The workshop content never fails to amaze me, even though there are some mods that aren't the best, and there's a lot of S.A.I.L replacement mods.
You can easily learn a bit ablut a material, because S.A.I.L tells you about when you first obtain it, it also can help in missions a bit.
The abandoned mine that you can find on your starter planet can make for a good early game challenge, and also as good rewards, like more than enough crystal shards to go to the outpost.
Cons:
Even though the colonies are pretty cool, I can never really find a good plot of flat land due to the mountainous generation of most planets, so I end up mining entire mountains so that I can make a town.
there's this bug that I encounter, I'm not entirely sure if it's a bug actually, but whenever i make a new character, usually after getting a large amount of new mods, I delete all my other characters, but the changes that the made to the outpost are still there. I figured out how to fix it, which is by deleting the everything in the universe folder thats in the storage folder.
The ruin, which is the final boss of starbound, isn't very difficult, i've had more trouble with earlier bosses, you can easily dodge 90% of the ruins attacks just by grappling to the ceiling of the boss room and shoting down at the ruins heart, the only attacks that pose a threat are any flying enemies that are spawned, which are really easy to kill since you have the best armor by the time you've gotten to the ruin.
A thing that I do'nt like about being on the first planet is that there's no way to get through smaller spaces without making them bigger. you can just crouch and spawm A or D, but that is just very tedious to do, same with making the holes bigger. your character should be able to crawl while crouching to get through at least 3 block tall spaces, or 2 block spawces but a bit slower, it would be good too or sneaking near enimies, so  you can ambush them, and do a large amount of damage before they can do much.
There isn't much good looking human furniture, Pretty much only play as a human, because I like to have a sorta spikey hair style, kinda like astro boy's, but hot pink, because why not, but the only real human furnature is stuff from a prison that doesn't look good in the town that I built, after flattening an entire mountain.
I hope you guys at Chucklefish at least consider doing something about the cons that are on this list, I, and maybe some other starbound players would really apreciate it. I do reccomend this game though, because it's a good game.

Think of a house. The house has good foundation and is located on a beautiful plot of land but is missing some of its windows and the plumbing isn’t finished yet. You walk inside this house and notice there's a couch and potted plant in the living room but not much else. You sit down on the couch and think to yourself "gee, this place is nice but could do with so much more". You walk back outside and see a contractor and ask him "This looks like it will be a great house someday! When are you finishing it?" to which the contractor responds by giving a fatigued sigh and taking his hardhat off his head before going "WE'RE WORKING ON IT!”
That is Street Fighter V currently.
I'm brand new to fighting games but have been having a blast with Street Fighter V currently despite getting my crap rekt almost every match I've played so far. You can mash buttons sure, but Street Fighter is most enjoyed as a tactical thinking game. Learning the moves, discovering what characters you like and dislike, predicting what your opponent is going to do next. It's all very rewarding and engaging once you get the basics down.
Of course one of the biggest cons that you will see with Street Fighter V is its current lack of content. There is very little single player to speak of at the moment and most of the game is obviously focused on the competitive scene and online play but Capcom has promised to expand upon the single player in the future. While it can be annoying at the moment I don't count this as a big con because I ultimately think Street Fighter V is an online game and what’s there is already very good. If a lack of single player doesn't sound that bad to you and you are looking for a challenging and competitive atmosphere I would heavily consider picking Street Fighter V. If not I would wait until a sale or until they add more content to make it a juicer game.
- Core fighting mechanics are rock solid, and what's there is already very good
- The game is gorgeous to look at, the art direction and style is spot on
- If you take time to invest in and learn the gameplay it is some of the most rich and rewarding feeling out there
- While small at the moment, the characters are extremely polished and each feel unique. You should have no trouble finding someone you will like.
- Feels unfinished
- While I haven't run into many of the problems which others claim to run into online it could use some polishing.
- Season Pass is probably going to be a must unless you have time or feel like grinding out for characters.
Street Fighter V is an excellent game that doesn't feel quite finished yet.
If you're into fighting games or Street Fighter already, pick this one up.
For everyone else, wait until a sale or until more content gets added.

WOW!  I played for over an hour without even knowing it!  This is a fun and well thought out game. I love the leveling system.  It's like Oblivion where you gain experience and levels from doing things.  There are many skills to level up, such as fighting, wood cutting, fishing, mining, farming, etc...  You can create almost anything once you have the tools and resources.  Everything is automatic once you start the process, such as fighting, which after three hits, you can retreat if needed. Other skills involve smelting raw materials, making molds for weapons and jewelry.  The list goes on and on!
It's easy to play and really is a great game so far.  I have not run into any glitches or bugs, but the game did crash when I quit. The only thing I can see people maybe not liking is that none of the sprites are animated.  It really doesn't hurt immersion as the game has so much going for it in all other areas!  I think it fits well.  It's like the old Ultima games, but much better!  It has a nice tutorial and what looks to be a fairly huge world to explore. They have events to join every now and then.
I didn't experience any lag or skipping.  It's a pretty polished game so far and it's really fun with so many things to do! AND it's free to play!  I have not once felt the need to purchase any extra cash with real $$$.
I recommend this game to anyone that likes well thought out RPG games! KUDOS to the developers!!!
Note: The game does require you to make an account and every character level you gain (not skill level) requires you to answer an anti-bot question to make sure you are not using auto-clicker software to play.

The community was dying with the game but the game still kept thousands of people active and participating. This is a true testament to how enjoyable (but many times unforgiving) this game really is. Now, Realm was acquired by a new company with grand ideas (Deca Games). This has not only breathed renewed interest in the game, but has a huge impact of the morale and attitude of the community. This game is now five years old and right now it seems to be getting stronger than ever with old players returning and new ones joining everyday. Overall, the gameplay is extremely tough at first, but if you stick with it and get through the heartbreaks of losing your precious characters, the game is extremely rewarding and exciting to experience. While there are still major problems with the game (such as multiboxers, hackers, and notifiers), the game really is looking up as Deca is not only hosting the absent Month of the Mad God (A yearly month long celebration) but also working overtime to ensure that justice is served to those that deserve it (the damn dupers). So, a 10/10 game (for me personally) because of our new saviors, Deca Games.

This is Christopher Nolan's 'Interstellar' all over again - I can't tell whether I love it, hate it or just don't care.
It's quite the depature from FO3 in terms of having the overall tone and RPG elements exchanged for far tighter combat and gameplay. You only have to walk a few feet in any direction to find a mission or 'scenario' unfolding and while this makes it far more accessible and satisfying in the short term, I never really felt like I was undertaking a real 'role in the universe'.
In FO4, I feel like I'm not discovering hidden treasures in a wasteland so much as picking through treasures that were specifically put there for me to find. That said, I do find the characters, gameplay, crafting, building and missions themselves highly, highly entertaining and a significant, allbeit iterative improvement on FO3.
If this game had the ambition, cohesion and narrative diversity of New Vegas, it'd be the greatest in the series by a long shot. As it happens, I think it's a solid but small step forward for the franchise and while I love it when all the elements come together, I can't help but feel there's a massive missed opportunity when viewing the game as the sum of its parts.

Let me start off by saying that I’m a gay girl and that I’ve been eyeing this game ever since it got released in Japan, which was back in 2012.
Was the wait worth it?
Hell yes.
As another reviewer has mentioned, this story does have a very porny premise.  Two ghosts rope MC into playing yuri cupid for various couples in the school so that the ghosts can spy on them and learn how to make love to each other, as girls—yes, this is morally questionable no matter how you word it—but despite this, the story is not centered around sex at all.  Really.  It took me around 12 hours to reach the first nsfw scene, and all the way up those 12 hours, the story focuses on developing relationships, emotional connections, friendship.  Rather than sex being the focal point of the game, it feels very much like a beautiful culmination to everything that couple has experienced together up to that point—from the confessions, to the trials and tribulations of trying get their love reciprocated, their sense of stability after ironing out misunderstandings.
Also, while the whole “b-but we’re both girls!” may seem excessive at some points, homosexuality in Japan is still very much condemned.  But that’s one of the most refreshing things about this game: not only does the story touch upon real issues like social stigma and family expectations, but it also doesn’t write off the girl/girl romances as just a phase, like so many other works in yuri genre do.  One couple in particular discusses and plans their future together in the face of a homophobic society, and that really resonated with me.
As someone who has also tried out the Sono Hanabira series, which oversexualizes girls (and even glosses over the fact that one of them is a huge age gap student/teacher lol), I am very happy that this game doesn’t treat homosexuality as a joke or something just to fetishize.  I really felt like the story was reaching out to girls in similar situations, living in fear of condemnation yet still brave enough to face their feelings and look forward to a brighter future.
Setting aside my accolades for the story, the voice acting, art, and music are also superb.  The nsfw scenes are very tasteful, and despite the fact that the OST is about 12/13 tracks, the songs are catchy enough that I never felt bothered by it.
Conclusion: if you love girls, love girls loving girls, love a good story, please get this game.  It’s $30, yes, but there’s around 30 hours of gameplay, so it’s well worth the money.  You won’t regret it.

So this was something I ended up playing on a whim. I saw this mentioned the week or so leading up to the game by a few people and I decided to give it a try since they had a demo avaliable. I'm extremely glad I did because this ended up being one of the best visual novels I've read, with wonderful characters and an emotinal plot. Though the game is rated 18+ and does contain sex scenes it's quite tame overall, and really doesn't even factor in until around halfway through the game. I was also surprised how the game tackles the subject of relationships, it doesn't pretend that they happen overnight or without some stumbling blocks. I mean the story is still pretty fluffly overall (it's about lesbian ghosts that wanna spread the lesbian around a school, c'mon) but I still think it took the romances realistically for the most part. Anyhow, let's break down what the pros, cons and nit-picks bout this game real quick.
Pros:
-A great main character, Yuna was delightful throughout. Almost all of the characters (barring one or two minor examples) are well written
-Emotionally engaging story, I'll admit I teared up quite a few times
-Satisfying ending
-Extra scenes that open up once you complete the main story
-OST is good, even if there are only about 12 tracks.
-Game takes relationships surprisingly seriously.
Cons:
-Some of the couples are just not as interesting as others, and the game makes you follow every side story
-Title is kinda weird. I read why it's that way but it's still weird.
-There ain't much porn if that's what you're here for.
Nit-Picks:
-I wish there had been just a bit more drama. I love the story but half the time the main character is just sitting around waiting for stuff to happen
-While the extra scenes after the main story were a nice touch, they were kind of pointless overall, to be blunt. While it did flesh out the relationships between some characters a bit more, they didn't do much for me. I'd have much preferred it if they'd given each of the couples a "one month later" epilogue or something
-Some of those songs in the OST, while good, might get annoying once they play for the 50th time
-I wish the game was longer. Though this should probably be a pro, I think this is one of the best compliments you can give a game. I wish there was a sequel, anime, something,
-By the way, if these ghosts wanted to see girls doing it, they DO have the internet. Feels like they could've solved this problem in 10 minutes. (I know not really, but still)
Overall the game was a delight to play, and I hope more similar games come soon. I don't usually replay visual novels, but I get the feeling I'm probably going to replay this one in the upcoming weeks. If I was giving this game a rating I'd say it's a 9/10

The Walking Dead is an interactive episodic story-driven game where you play as Lee Everett, a convicted criminal who unknowningly becomes a survivor of a zombie apocolypse and given a second chance of life. He meets a child named Clementine who you are given the duty to take care of. Throughout the story, your actions and decisions determine on how the story will continue. The game is based of the (
) comic series by writer Robert Kirkman and artist Tony Moore. There are differences between the comic (which I haven't read lol) and the game which is more focused on character development.
For a game that's made in 2012, it's a bit...eh... It's definetely not horrible or fantastic but I can understand that they were going for graphics with a comic book style. To simply put, I'd say it's somewhat outdated but I had no problems in running the game whatsoever.
As this is an interactive game, you get to decide what Lee does and says which can affect the story in a good or bad way.
If you're looking forward to some action, it's not going to be too dramatic as there are some factors which you need to use your brain a lot more to think if what you're doing is a wise decision. Despite me not playing more than 8+ hours of this game, if you're not into games with a deep story, then this may not be a pleasant experience for you, especially those who are confused and don't know what to do without a guide or walkthrough.
The music gets the atmosphere to feel tense and is pretty good to listen to. It adds more emotion to the major scenes that gives you real impact on the characters who are surviving the apocolypse. Other than that, there's not much to say to be honest.
The Walking Dead is great story driven game that focuses on the decisions you made and the characters you meet. It gets you to think more wisely as if it were a real zombie apocolypse. It may not be for gamers who are into high, intense all time action but for those who are into interactive, story games, this is game that'll look great in your collection.

It's a GTA inspired cover shooter with Arkham City style melee combat. It tries to combine a lot of influences, and I believe that gameplay wise it works. But in an effort to create a more serious story, it did away with a lot of the style of the games it tried to emulate.
The story is worthwhile, but there's not much to keep you playing after you finish it. In an open world sandbox game, this is somewhat disappointing. The extra story DLC gives you more of a reason to stay. But all those side missions that you would find compelling in other games are not that entertaining. The city and most of its characters are pretty similar throughout. And while the game tries to make you feel like your actions have an impact on the emotional state of the main character, the nature of the game allows you to do whatever you want with no repercussions.
Controls are tight and gameplay is fair (if a little on the easy side). I've never found myself complaining if I died or lost a mission, since it's clear why it is that it happened. The combat system is not that difficult to master, and after you do you feel like an invincible badass. The game makes it clear that guns are rare, so you'll mostly be beating people up with your kung-fu and any environmental attacks that you can find. These environmental attacks are visually compelling but grisly, usually killing whomever you used them against. Again, it contrasts with what the story is trying to tell you about the main character, but it's a welcome addition to gameplay.
If you can get the game on the cheap, it's worth playing. Gameplay is tight, and the main story is told well. It's also worth it to buy the story extending DLC, which adds to the substance and humor that was missing in the main game. The rest of the DLC is not worth it, mostly consisting of extra clothing and vehicles which don't serve much of a purpose in game.

Are there worse disappointments in grown-up life than Street Fighter V?  Of course, but it's so maxed out on the scale of video game disappointments I can only liken it to real life disappointments.  You know that old adage that sex is like pizza, even when it's bad its good?  Street Fighter V is like the sex that isn't like pizza.  The kind you immediately regret and are pretty sure is gonna make you sick.
If there isn't going to be an offline tournament mode, then the servers need to be vaguely functional.  Am I too old?  Is this an age thing?  The offline tournament mode to me has always been "the game."  Sure I enjoy playing online against other players, but after I beat the "the game."  So that part being omitted feels like I spent $80 on the preorder and season pass to actually not even get what I consider to be the core game itself.  I've tried to keep an open mind though, because maybe this is an age thing.  Maybe I'm wrong here.  So I really tried to dive deep into the online mode, but the servers are just terrible. It takes 5-10 minutes on average to find a match.  I have to play something else while I wait and by the time it queues up, I'm not really in the moment anymore.  Another big disappointment is that I love the big cast of characters, but they cut way back.  Street Fighter IV added so many classic characters to what I thought was going to be the permanent lexicon of SF.
This game feels really thin and flimsy.  I'm not even addressing the ragequit exploit, because Capcom promises severe punishment.  If you're putting all your eggs in one basket, doubling down on online tournament play only, then doesn't that seem like a really basic, careless, obvious misstep?  That's the kind of lack of attention to detail and quality that permeates every aspect of this game.
I'm pretty sure this only gets read by my friends.  If that is the case and you're reading this, then please come over and play this game any time you want before actually spending money on it.  I'll make time for you.  That's how bad this is.  I would rather rearrange my schedule than see my friends get screwed by this as I have been.

I was first introduced to Super Giant Games by my friend, via the new game Transistor. Skeptical, because we don't share all of the same game tastes, I sat down to try it out. I was actually blown away by how good it was, and how fun it was to play, and so I looked for it online. Sadly, it was not on Mac (and I made awful computer decisions), but the similar spiritual predecessor 'Bastion' was!
A few hours into the game, and I've fallen in love with it. The combat is fluid and excellently designed, the levels are fun to navigate, with plenty of secrets for those gamers who love to explore, and the various weapons make it so any playstyle can fit. I think my favorite part of the game is how rewarding it feels. You'll be strolling along, making an easy time of the mobs that attack, and suddenly you'll be surrounded on all sides. The game changes from leisurely to pulse-pounding in a matter of seconds, and the feeling after beating a particularly hard level is akin to that of beating a Dark Souls boss (though much less difficult).
It's not really a platformer, and it's relatively linear. The voice acting from the narrator keeps you interested the whole time, and you won't believe the sheer amount of dialogue actually placed in the game (i.e., narrator has something to say if you've fallen off the stage 3 times, or something). If I had one complaint, it would be that at a certain point in the game, you feel like you're just retracing your steps, without even re-visiting key areas. The plot is shadowed by the fact that much of the story is revealed along the way, and you're not entirely sure who you are in this strange world, and what you're meant to be doing. Definitely worth the purchase, especially if you can't get Transistor yet, but I highly recommend both games.

Similar to Nickervision's previous titles, Bit Blaster XL and Orbt XL, Diamo XL is another easy-to-learn simple score-attack arcade game. Complete with an optional tutorial and an immediate restart option upon game over, the game's pace and flow is steady and consistent.
The gameplay is simple; using the four directional inputs (up, down, left, right), you guide your character to a point on the diamond grid. Once you start moving, you can't stop until you reach the next node, so timing is needed to avoid the enemy projectiles. The goal of the game is to traverse all 8 paths of the diamond grid to score points, then repeat the process indefinitely while avoiding red enemy projectiles that hover over the map. After game over, you're presented with numerous detailed statistics about your playthrough, such as amount of time spent idle, number of diamonds completed, close calls, etc. as well as the option to tweet your score, compare your score to others on the global leaderboard, try again or return to the main menu.
The game rewards you with a higher score multiplier the longer you go without moving, and there's a cooldown for said combo multiplier as to not make the gameplay feel too rushed or hectic. Similar to Bit Blaster and Orbt, the difficulty starts out easy then scales to be more difficult the higher your score gets; more enemy projectiles on screen, new enemies that disable sections of the grid for a short period of time, etc. The game also rewards you with different "characters" to choose from, and they're unlocked simply by playing the game; the more you play, the more points you earn, and each character's unlocking criterion (i.e. Earn X points in total) is shown in the character select screen.
I played this game with my Xbox360 Afterglow USB controller and had no issues, and there's an option to disable controller rumble in the options. If the catchy music track isn't to your liking or you're getting tired of it, you can also disable it (and sound effects) in the options menu and just play your own music in the background instead.
In conclusion, Diamo XL plays exactly how it's presented. The content, gameplay and replayability make Diamo XL worth its low price, especially if it goes on sale.

Blackwake, and honest, fair review.
I'm pretty skeptical about many Early Access titles. especially Alpha games. This game is different though.
Everything is very balanced, and teamwork is very important. There is no way in hell you could manage a ship on your own.
What is this?
Blackwake is a Naval Team FPS focused on Navy VS Pirate combat in open waters. There are a plethora of modes, but the dominant one currently is TDM. (Team DeathMatch). There are many different weathers and even the time of the day will change occasionaly. You will be assigned one of many roles by a captain that you vote up at the start of the round. You could be running supplies to people, fixing holes caused by opposing ships, and even shoot cannons! Be sure to listen to the captain though, as he has the final decision on the ship and can kick you off if you don't listen.
What stands out in Blackwake?
The community and combat really give this game its name. They're always willing to help, and for such a low playerbase currently there is still full servers that are played on frequently. People love to sound like actual pirates and Navy men. The combat? Ohmyyyyygodddd it's so satisfying. Loading a cannon, and firing at an enemy ship, killing 3 people and sending the ship down. Ramming is done great and is filled with action. You could be below deck when you randomly here a big, powerful explosion of wood and water flying everywhere. Holes appear, maybe the nose of your ship breaks, and a storm of oppenents rush the ship. Everything about it really gives it fun.
You really like to give the game a good name. Now tell me the cons.
It's in EA. Infact, Alpha! It's very early in development, but the developers really work on their game to balance and add stuff. There's updates pretty much weekly. There is the fair share of bugs though, but the majority is clipping. You won't have to deal with it much though. I wish there were more players, and maybe larger servers for more ship to ship combat. A lot of the other modes aren't as populated, while they are a fair share of fun. The learning curve? Not too steep, but you still will have a challenge getting into the game initially.
The Pros?

-Combat
-Atmosphere
-Effects
-Communication
-Very Team based (Depends... Could be a con if you like to play solo)

What is Bastion? Well for me it was not only a game, but also an experience like Journey, Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons and other similar games. An experience that I will always remember.
The gameplay is pretty simple: you move around the isometric maps and kill enemies and occasional bosses using a variety of melee and long range weapons. A more interesting twist is that later on you can set difficulty level you want by activating up to ten shrines that give various buffs to your enemies. Playing certain levels with all of the shrines active can be quite challenging. There is also a "New Game+" option when you finish the game and since it has multiple ending it can be worth having second playthrough.
The visuals are very nice. Each level is beautifully drawn and the level builds up under your feet as you move which makes the overall look even more appealing.
The sounds. There are two sides worth mentioning. The music and the Stranger. The music is really good and fits the game great. I'd probably think about buying it if I hadn't gotten it together with Bastion in the Humble Bundle.
The Stranger is this games most known feature. He is the narrator that talks about you and your journey with a deep and very nice voice. He is so popular they even made a Bastion announcer for Dota 2.
All in all this game will probably leave a lasting memory and is a great experience. I have really enjoyed playing it and it's definitely worth it's price. I would definitely recommend you to try Bastion. You will not regret it.

Being someone who has invested over 560 hours into this game I have come to a conclusion and I want to leave my opinion on the game. These will look over various points.
1.Main Questline:
Now, I am fully aware of the get quest,kill things, get thing, get reward cycle, but in my opinion, the Main Questline is a ton of fun to play. It allows for a sense of relief and the ending is so climactic ending with a bang. However, the main story is incredibly lackluster, doesn't have many twists and I believe that some of the side quests are more memorable. There are only two quests that sparked my attention when playing the main questline: Unlikely Valentine and The Nuclear Option/Nuclear Family. This is because the climactic ending of The Nuclear Option/Nuclear Family is amazing but could have more work and Unlikely Valentine has the most interesting character introduced (Detective Nick Valentine). All the other quests didn't really give me any reason to remember them.
2.Side Quests:
The side quests in this game are awesome. Be it helping a rocket powered ship take off or finding a delusional man with a strange alien artifact the games side quests are great. However the side quests that really stood out to me are: The Last Voyage of The USS Constitution, The Cabot Family Questline, The Silver Shroud, Detective Case Files and Pickman's gallery Quest. These are all incredibly unique to the fallout franchise. Where else are you going to pretend you are a superhero with a silver tommy gun and kill drug dealers?
3.Replayability:
With 566 hours clogged into this game, I have many, many different characters, all different builds, all unique. The game allows great customisability with your characters. Be it a stelathy ninja, a knight in power armour or a sadistic lunatic who eats people, you can be who you wanna be. The game offers tons and tons of random encounters. meaning the place you go to will always be different. You can play this game for hours on end.
4.Factions:
Terrible. You either be a xenophobic self-rightous gang, a freedom fighting xenophobic gang, scientist slavers or a group of civillians who can't shut up about settlements. 2 are the same, 1 is evil and 1 always needs your help. Take your pick.
5.Companions:
Terrible again. Apart from nick valentine, dogmeat or the robots you can make in automatron. I don't use any of the other companions, maybe cait but that's it. The affinity system is good but can be annoying, frustrating and downright horrid at times.
6.Settlement System:
Not bad. But, it doesn't just work. Settlers don't assign, There is a space LIMIT, and some settlers can't be moved.
7. Creation Club:
You know I had to mention this. First off, You don't have to use the creation club or pay for it. Second, It isn't paid mods, it is a buisness practice to make addons and pay mod makers the money they rightfully deserve. Lastly, again you don't HAVE to use it, it is just an option.
8.Mods:
Speaks for itself really.
9.Overall:
If anyone wants a great post-apocalyptic first person shooter. Then Fallout 4 may not be perfect but is a damn good example of how fun games can be. 6.5/10

My main points after playing the game myself mirror portions of multiple other reviewer's:
- Agree somewhat with reviewer that said it feels a lot like "Mass Effect but restricted to only the Normandy". It does have a bit of that feel to it, but I would say there's more to it than that description since the entirety of Consortium's story progression is on the ship itself. Perhaps more akin to a compressed Mass Effect where the whole story takes place within the confines of the Normandy, and with only limited time spent on pure combat.
- Despite lots of patches there are still bugs. Lots of them. Some are humourous, some are mildly annoying, some are hellishly frustrating, and some are game-breaking and require a reload to progress beyond. My experience after 2 full start-to-finish playthroughs and half-a-playthrough-worth of reloading to experience alternative decision trees was most definitely diminished by bugs, but not enough that I didn't still really enjoy the overall experience.
- The game is indeed somewhat of a "blue balls" experience. There's a solid 5-10 hours of enjoyable story-centric gameplay in a game-universe which did a good job of pulling me in, but you can really see that the game isn't quite fully fleshed out in multiple areas. Combat has some promise, but is barely utilised outside of a training simulator thing. The story has many --most would say too many-- loose ends and unanswered question which are not tied up even if you go to the trouble of investigating additional dialogue and backstory. It ends on a cliffhanger right when you expect to get more answers. What exists is not bad and it's not unejoyable. It really feels like they're (intentionally or not) showing the player "dude look at how much potential we have here - look at <X, Y, Z, all actually implemented to some functional degree in the game>, help us make the sequel everything it can be!"
- Graphics aren't great and the game isn't well optimised. Load times are on the longer side given the asset quality and the same goes for performance in-game.
- The story is quite engaging, supported by reasonably good voice acting across over a dozen characters. Decision trees are fairly broad, if only moderately deep on average (which I don't strike against it considering the breadth). As I discovered when playing through a second time with someone else, if you're mid-conversation with a character and then walk away, they'll react to the fact that you're walking away / being a♥♥♥♥♥♥
Would I recommend it? Yeah, absolutely, and I already have to a few people. I enjoyed most of the time I spent on this game - I just hope the sequel can adequately address the first game's problems.

As a massive yuri fan, I'm really excited about this game being on steam. After playing, A Kiss for Petals - Remembering You, I really needed a new Yuri/Shoujo-Ai game to play and this filled that slot perfectly.
This is also the first uncensored visual novel on steam; however, the story does not center itself around this concept, but on the interesting interactions between the characters themseles. The scenes themselves are actually quite tastefull and fit with the game's character driven storyline.
Kindred Spirits on the roof is an innovative and refreshing take on the visual novel genre; therefore, I would recomend anyone buying this game to both be preprared for and understand what type of game it actually is.
You play as a slightly anti-social girl who, while eating alone on the roof, discovers two ghosts and is then draged into playing match-maker for a variety of different yuri couples.
The purpose of the game is to create a Yuritopia!
What else do you need to know about it to XD
As of this moment, I have completely cleared Kindred Spirits on the Roof XD
The only real problem that I had with the game was the fact that steam overlay does not work and therefore I could not take recordings or screenshots; however, despite this the game was so good that I ended up losing a few days sleep.
Despite having only one ending, the game has a massive amount of extra content after the initial storyline ends. Extra content is garnered by choosing different dialogue options when they are presented towards you; however, as previously mentioned, the game only has one ending so your choices do not actually affect the main game.
On the subject of characters, I was actually quite suprised by quite a few characters in this game as well as how my opinions on them shifted later on. There were about two or three characters I just did not connect with, but there were also quite a few a characters that I initialy disliked who ended up being some of my favorites. I actually wish that a few of these characters had gotten a bit more time spent on them, but there is always the possibility of a sequel....maybe.
The art style was about mid-range for me, but it was a lot better than I was expecting and actually complimented the game's other elements quite well.
The ending, which I will not spoil, brought everything to a close quite well.
Overall this was quite a great game and I would deffinitly recommend it to those who enjoy yuri and/or visual novels.

I would like to point out, that I haven't played with Sanctum 1 so my review will based on my first impressions with the franchise.
If you just like maze building, and enjoying towers do all the work, then avoid this game, you will be disappointed.
But if you're looking for a good mixture of FPS and tower defense, where you actively fend off mobs yourself, then Sanctum 2 is  for you. The game is fun in solo, but you will have a great time in CO-OP with a good party. There's a wide variety of maps, monsters, towers and weapons. The game has a big replay value thanks to the Survival and Sandbox modes.
LIKE:
- Fairly entertaining story for a tower defense game
- Solid  CO-OP system, with great difficulty scaling, that puts your team work to the test.
- Good variety of monsters, towers and maps
- Bosses offer a good challange.
- Leveling system with unlockable perks and weapons to customize your character's skills.
- Secret areas with mini games.
- Replayability thanks to the Feats of Strenght system, Survival and Sandbox mode.
(- Funny text to speech option.)
DISLIKE (mostly minor issues):
- Character models could be more detailed
- Menu, and score screen could be more polished
- Map glitches which make your character stuck. Happens at 1-2 spots on certain maps.
Pretty fun and scarry. 10/10

Are there worse disappointments in grown-up life than Street Fighter V?  Of course, but it's so maxed out on the scale of video game disappointments I can only liken it to real life disappointments.  You know that old adage that sex is like pizza, even when it's bad its good?  Street Fighter V is like the sex that isn't like pizza.  The kind you immediately regret and are pretty sure is gonna make you sick.
If there isn't going to be an offline tournament mode, then the servers need to be vaguely functional.  Am I too old?  Is this an age thing?  The offline tournament mode to me has always been "the game."  Sure I enjoy playing online against other players, but after I beat the "the game."  So that part being omitted feels like I spent $80 on the preorder and season pass to actually not even get what I consider to be the core game itself.  I've tried to keep an open mind though, because maybe this is an age thing.  Maybe I'm wrong here.  So I really tried to dive deep into the online mode, but the servers are just terrible. It takes 5-10 minutes on average to find a match.  I have to play something else while I wait and by the time it queues up, I'm not really in the moment anymore.  Another big disappointment is that I love the big cast of characters, but they cut way back.  Street Fighter IV added so many classic characters to what I thought was going to be the permanent lexicon of SF.
This game feels really thin and flimsy.  I'm not even addressing the ragequit exploit, because Capcom promises severe punishment.  If you're putting all your eggs in one basket, doubling down on online tournament play only, then doesn't that seem like a really basic, careless, obvious misstep?  That's the kind of lack of attention to detail and quality that permeates every aspect of this game.
I'm pretty sure this only gets read by my friends.  If that is the case and you're reading this, then please come over and play this game any time you want before actually spending money on it.  I'll make time for you.  That's how bad this is.  I would rather rearrange my schedule than see my friends get screwed by this as I have been.

There's a lot to say about GOCCO, and yet there's very little to say about it at the same time. So let me just start with a couple stuff... pointless and trivial stuff that you may or may not find yourself asking.
** Skip to the bottom for TL:DR summary.
First, why is it called "GOCCO OF WAR" when the game's actual title, "Global Online Chibi Combat Offensive", while more of a mouthful, sounds less stupid than GOCCO OF WAR?
Second, why is the game purely co-operative, when it has the assets to create a pvp option as well? The game even has you shooting at other "children" during many of the 20... well, 23 stages.
Third, why is this game so grindy? For a casual, non-pvp game, getting badges and creating weapons requires a large investment of time, moreso than games like Monster Hunter do. It's not even fun half the time, especially when you, as the player, realize that every enemy is in a fixed location, and the only variation between runs is the pattern in which the AI moves.
Fourth, Enemy AI can be cheated out if you stand on a lower ledge of thin platforms.
Fifth, If a gun has a long barrel(such a gatling gun), the player can clip the gun through thin walls and shoot enemies through them.
Sixth, Despite the game's many costumes, most of them are just recolors-- why not just make 100+ costumes that are unique and can be colored any way the player wishes, instead of having 300 costumes, 5 of which are recolors of the same costume, totalling less than the 100 individual ones overall?
The game is only as fun for as long as you are playing with friends or other people. GOCCO of war quickly becomes stale if you are playing it alone, unless you like grinding for costumes. Quests can be done solo or in a group, with enemies scaling to the amount of players present. Let's face it, though, will you really replay all the stages again without friends, unless you're grinding out specific mats? Highly unlikely.
GOCCO has little replayability, which is why it has to be masked with endless grinding for S rank badges, materials, and money. Having played it for at least 35 hours, I feel it's fair enough for me to say something along those lines. Peakvox played it safe and made the game PVE only, which isn't a bad thing, but they had little updates. For a game centralized around PVE to have no meaningful updates, its death was sealed to be far earlier than most.
Had there been a PVP option to GOCCO OF WAR, I assume that would have extended its lifespan by about a year or two, maybe more if it was secretly a hardcore game, but there is none. With the addition of PVP, the game would become a lot more toxic with infestations of upstuck memers and other unsavory personalities. That's a risk most companies must take if they wish for longevity for their game. Also, speaking from experience, the game can be pretty balanced pvp-wise, as there are solutions for everything-- every weapon type has its strengths and weaknesses. With minor balancing, GOCCO OF WAR could be very successful as a PVP game.
As it stands, GOCCO OF WAR is a ghost town-- much like the hidden lore to the game. As far as I remember, GOCCO OF WAR's setting takes place in
. Of course, I feel like I was reading too deeply into the things various NPCs have said, and it might not be that bleak, but hey... would be pretty cool, right?
I'm giving this game a thumbs down, simply because the game's pricetag in comparison to its content and replayability just don't agree. The game's only about 10 hours tops if you take the time to grind a little for better equipment, but aside from that, it's incredibly short. For me, $1 means 1 hour of play, and asking me to play for 20 hours is really quite demanding. Fortunately, I had friends to play it with, and the game was pretty active when I was playing. Usually about 100 people on at any given time, even the late hours of night. Fortunately, I got this game on sale, so I definitely got my money's worth out of it... while it lasted.
Anyway, TL:DR - The game's a literal ghost town, both in lore and in community. Don't play it unless you have a group of friends (1-3), or if you like mindless grinding for materials to make costumes and weapons that no one but yourself will admire anymore due to how empty the server(s) are.

A fun open world arcade racer that overcomplicates the racing elements while over simplifying all the customization options.
-A fairly large & open world to explore
-Collectibles

-Steam Version is incomplete & Missing DLC
-Online Modes have Cheaters
-Can't Customize Cars
-Requiares EA Account Log-In
I guess you could call this game an open world collectathon with races & challenges as your objectives.  It's a very good concept but some parts weren't really executed properly.  For one, it's hard to figure out where exactly you are in the world & where you need to go in races.  Most racing games have you on a set track but this game all the tracks are connected & if you mess up by making a wrong turn you're pretty much screwed. To actually race you need to memorize the world map for the best routes to take in each race & it's just not worth it for the minimal rewards you get for doing it.  Each race is set up so you drive to the starting point, press a button & start the race.  The problem with this is you have absolutely no idea where you're going or the routes you need to take to get there.  It will take you several tries just to find & win the simplest of tracks because of the huge lack of direction you're given.  The game does try to help you by using the blinker on your car to tell you when there's an upcoming turn at least but it's not nearly enough.  I constantly find myself trying to do races & getting lost during them simply because of how lack of direction there is in this game.
The plus side is the Road Rage races, where direction is not really needed.  You just need to take out as many other racers as you can within the time limit while reaching the set goal.  This is probably the best challenge in the game since you don't need to figure out where to go & just drive.
There are also things in the world to collect & find such as hidden pathways, cars to take down that add themselves to your collection & bill boards.  I don't know if you actually get anything for doing 100% since I don't care enough about this game to 100% collect everything in it.  Most of what it seemed relatively pointless, honestly, with the exception of the car unlocks.
You can customize certain cars but only the type of color & paint job, e.g. Metalic, gloss, etc.  The motorcycles let you pick between Male/Female riders but that's about it. That's really all you can do cuztomization wise.
There's also an abundance of cheaters in online modes.  Just recently I had a game with at least two cheaters who were both using cheats that gave them instant take downs & made them immune to take downs.  Basically, this means that whenever they just barely tapped my car or anyone elses we'd be taken down & even if we rammed them through a wall they'd never be taken down.  Their takedown score was around 10x what everyone elses was the entire match.  And trust me, I played with these two long enough to know they were cheating.  I only wish I was recording at the time so I could show all the BS that was going on.
There's also a small amount of people who actually play online now.  I played this game for several hours recently & got into about 4 games but each game I was in one of those two cheaters were always in one.  So, in the end I just accepted that I wasn't gonna be playing to win & just ended up goofing off with the hackers for a few hours.  There also is no report system in the game so if someone is cheating you can't do anything about it.  The only thing you can do is try to deal with it or leave the online mode.
You also can't get the DLC content through Steam since EA is a bunch of D-bags.  They cut off the EA marketplace so even though you're buying the "Ultimate Box" you're getting an incomplete product.  To make matters worse the online shop will constantly pop up every time you boot up the game, but it will just load a blank white screen.  So, it taunts you saying, "Yea, this game is missing features.  Thanks for buying it, sucker!"  You can get the DLC buy claiming your copy on EA's Origin & then buying it to add to your account.  You may need to open a ticket & have a customer service rep help you, though.
Overall, this game is fun but it's really not worth anyone's time anymore unless you just want a driving game to goof off with. The online modes have hackers & the whole game takes too long to figure out & memorize, plus the missing DLC doesn't help matters much.  If you want a real racing experience that doesn't just involve driving around in an open world where you just crash cars you'd be better off trying something else.  If not, then feel free to try this one cause crashing cars & driving around doing random nonsense is the best part about this game.  It's a fun & fast arcade racer at it's core.

Blackwake, and honest, fair review.
I'm pretty skeptical about many Early Access titles. especially Alpha games. This game is different though.
Everything is very balanced, and teamwork is very important. There is no way in hell you could manage a ship on your own.
What is this?
Blackwake is a Naval Team FPS focused on Navy VS Pirate combat in open waters. There are a plethora of modes, but the dominant one currently is TDM. (Team DeathMatch). There are many different weathers and even the time of the day will change occasionaly. You will be assigned one of many roles by a captain that you vote up at the start of the round. You could be running supplies to people, fixing holes caused by opposing ships, and even shoot cannons! Be sure to listen to the captain though, as he has the final decision on the ship and can kick you off if you don't listen.
What stands out in Blackwake?
The community and combat really give this game its name. They're always willing to help, and for such a low playerbase currently there is still full servers that are played on frequently. People love to sound like actual pirates and Navy men. The combat? Ohmyyyyygodddd it's so satisfying. Loading a cannon, and firing at an enemy ship, killing 3 people and sending the ship down. Ramming is done great and is filled with action. You could be below deck when you randomly here a big, powerful explosion of wood and water flying everywhere. Holes appear, maybe the nose of your ship breaks, and a storm of oppenents rush the ship. Everything about it really gives it fun.
You really like to give the game a good name. Now tell me the cons.
It's in EA. Infact, Alpha! It's very early in development, but the developers really work on their game to balance and add stuff. There's updates pretty much weekly. There is the fair share of bugs though, but the majority is clipping. You won't have to deal with it much though. I wish there were more players, and maybe larger servers for more ship to ship combat. A lot of the other modes aren't as populated, while they are a fair share of fun. The learning curve? Not too steep, but you still will have a challenge getting into the game initially.
The Pros?
I'm going to listen these, for the sake of your reading time.
-Graphics (Very splendid, realistic.
-Community
-Combat
-Atmosphere
-Effects
-Communication
-Very Team based (Depends... Could be a con if you like to play solo)
-Active Developers (They listen to request)
-And a great future ahead.
My rating?
5/7 - Perfect score.
Just kidding
9.5/10 (Get it while it's on sale! Quite a steal!)
Thank you for reading.
See you on the water.

As a big Street Fighter fan, I couldnt rezist to buy this new game in the series.
However, I should warn anyone who is interested in Single Player mode mostly that there isnt really any like it was in the previous games except the Survival mode which is not Arcade mode by any means.
Capcom will add Arcade mode and more content later this year, so if you are looking for a Single Player experience you should wait with your purchase. The game will be cheaper by that time aswell. The game also lacks from basic things like rebinding your keys, shop is not implemented yet and so on. As it stands for now, it is a pure online experience with the possibility of a training mode and the above mentioned Survival mode but thats it.
But fighting games were always focused around fighting other players, where you can show off your skill in a local or multiplayer session. Multiplayer is a very good experience in Street Fighter 5. And thats why I bought it in the first place.
Cross platform multiplayer is a thing now. You can play against players who play on their PS4. Which is a big deal, because the community wont split and will make a big player base in total.
Characters in the future will be added, and they will be accesed for free. Costumes and things like that will be able for purchase using fightmoney which you receive for playing the game. Some costumes will maybe cost real money, but it doesnt affect gameplay at all.
The last important thing worth mentioning is that there will be no more editions of Street Fighter 5 like it was in the past. SF4, SF4 Arcade edition, Ultimate SF4 etc. This is the only version of SF5 which will exist. Capcom dont want to split up their player base using different versions of the game. So those who are waiting for an ultimate edition released later with all the characters and costumes, well.... dont wait. There wont be any. This is the version which will be updated all the time.
A lot of the mechanics has been changed, reworked, removed and new things were added. So for an experienced SF player it still requires some learning curve. I find this game to be more difficult than SF4 or even SF 3 Third Strike.
For a Street Fighter fan, this is a must have. For the casual players who are looking for an arcade mode, hold on until capcom adds more content. The music and the graphics are also amazing and typical for a SF game.

This is a large MMORPG with an isometric tileset, which was very popular in the 90's.  It can be played from almost anywhere: client, website, Mac, PC, Linux, Android, iOS, etc.  It's a small install (if you use a client), and it uses hardly any system resources.
The game is a freemium game, but it is not cursed with a Pay To Win culture.  MOS is a currency that you can buy with real money or earn in-game and spend on special items, extra bank spaces, Market spaces, etc.
The world is split into areas named after Estonian towns: You start in Tutorial Island, but then truly begin in Dorpat.  From there, you can travel via jump points or teleport scrolls & potions to other maps like Reval, Rakblood, Whiland, Walco, etc.  Additionally, there are varying dungeons and towers, No Man's Land is a dangeous PVP area, Arena is a tournament/Dual Arena mashup that allows betting, etc.  The world is big!
Skills correspond well to Runescape, with significant improvements.
Combat skills (Accuracy, Strength, Defense, Hit Points, Health, Magic, Archery)
Gathering skills (Farming, Woodcutting, Fishing, etc)
Artisanal skills (Jewelry, Fletching, Cooking, Forging, Breeding (pet creation)
Combat:
Melee combat is a lot like RS07, able to use controlled, aggressive, etc
Ranged combat keeps your opponents from hitting you at all.
Magic is based off of scrolls and pouches.
You can dual-wield a 1h weapon and magic like Skyrim for high DPS.
2x Exp is a potion that you can buy or is provided for top-level donators.  When triggered, the entire world gets 2x xp for a period of time.  So, most people use gatherer skills during 1x and artisanal skills during 2x.
Party Quests are groups of up to 4 people who go on one of two timed missions:
-Kill a set number of monsters in a set time period
-Wade through monsters, find 3 keys, and open a large chest.
Not only do you get the drops, but if you complete the mission, you get extra stuff like MOS or coins.
There are skill quests and group quests, but there is no lore in the game.
Skill quests are offered by Skill Masters in groups of 10 that refresh every hour.  The more you do ,the better they get.  Rewards vary from coins, items, MOS, or experience.
Combat quests are linear, auto-assigned upon finishing one, and become harder and longer as you progress.  Same rewards as above.
You can purchase a personal island.  There, you can build a house, bed, furniture, a ship to travel to other player-owned islands, decorations, etc.  However, most use them for Farming, Breeding, and Fletching.
The economy is well-designed.  Most basic and low-level items can be bought and sold directly with NPCs stationed in most towns.  All else can be bought and sold to/from other players via the Market, a place to list items at whatever price you choose.  Surprisingly, there is little price manipulation.
You bank and access the Market at chests.
You start with 60 chest spaces.  Extras come in packs of 60 and costs 500k or I think 50 MOS.  Unlike some other games, the Chest places your items in a predictable location and also has sorting tools to make it easy to find items.
The anti-botting system is brilliant.
It uses Google CAPTCHA checks.  If you pass, you get a point that gives extra exp in the skill of your choice.  If you fail, you lose a point.  Hit -5 and you get thrown in jail until a GM or developer (think JMOD) can talk to you and decide your fate.
The greatest thing about this game is the community.
People are incredibly helpful, everyone is friendly, rude people get shut down quickly in main chat.  Developers stop into the main chat often to check in.  Margus, the guy who made the game, pops into main chat and talks with everyone.
In short, this game has been a massive surprise, and I plan to play it for quite some time.
I think Realm has vastly improved over the last few weeks, Deca has breathed brand new life into the game and I'm excited to see what's to come.

What is Bastion? Well for me it was not only a game, but also an experience like Journey, Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons and other similar games. An experience that I will always remember.
The gameplay is pretty simple: you move around the isometric maps and kill enemies and occasional bosses using a variety of melee and long range weapons. A more interesting twist is that later on you can set difficulty level you want by activating up to ten shrines that give various buffs to your enemies. Playing certain levels with all of the shrines active can be quite challenging. There is also a "New Game+" option when you finish the game and since it has multiple ending it can be worth having second playthrough.
The visuals are very nice. Each level is beautifully drawn and the level builds up under your feet as you move which makes the overall look even more appealing.
The sounds. There are two sides worth mentioning. The music and the Stranger. The music is really good and fits the game great. I'd probably think about buying it if I hadn't gotten it together with Bastion in the Humble Bundle.
The Stranger is this games most known feature. He is the narrator that talks about you and your journey with a deep and very nice voice. He is so popular they even made a Bastion announcer for Dota 2.
All in all this game will probably leave a lasting memory and is a great experience. I have really enjoyed playing it and it's definitely worth it's price. I would definitely recommend you to try Bastion. You will not regret it.

Rating based on current state of play, as per my last login. The last time I logged in, there was nearly no one to play with, things were stagnating, and there was far less to do as a "greenie" (nonsubscriber on subscriber oceans) than there seemed to have felt like in the past. Even if I had resub'd, there didn't see that much to do, let alone anyone to do any of it with.
I played Y!PP on and off for SO. SO. SO. many years. I believe my first account was made somewhere in 05 to 06, putting me at roughly the 9-10 year mark. While I played more off than on, those times during which I did play I would get completely sucked back into my ocean for weeks, if not months.
When I was a bit younger, this game was tremendous amounts of fun. This has more to do with the fact that the ocean(s) were far more populated back then than they are these days, even after the colossal oceans merge. I was originally on Cobalt I believe, which during the prime of my play-days was THE ocean to be on. As I got older, I began to better understand the mechanics of the games I was actually playing, which made me better at them - but, alas, there weren't many people to play with anymore.
The puzzles themselves are clever and a LOT of fun. Most of them are simple enough to begin with that anyone could jump right in; still, they also have layers of depth enough to keep amused those whom understand the advanced concepts to each (insane amounts of chaining, combos out the booty, etc etc).
The variety of things to do seemed pretty much endless for awhile. From jobbing to running pillages; sloshing down drinks and throwing down rounds of poker, hearts, spades; exploring uninhabited islands; playing borderline-impossible games of hide-and-seek with me mates and trying to make everyone play on the fair (aka clickable; looking at you, dock arrow hiders!); running a shoppe; blockading islands; and so much more. There are so many awesome puzzles sprawled all across the game, and they are all extremely unique. You can spend hours working on your ability to perform Incredibles on one of the half dozen or more ship/duty puzzles; then go manage your shoppe/stalls and put in work hours at the awesome crafting puzzles; then spend a couple hours running commodities from port to port; go in search of El Polo Diablo for kicks and giggles and much insta death lols; then chill out at the tavern with drinks, game puzzles, swordfighting duels, and players buying, selling, trading, looking or advertising for crews, trying to pick a fight, and more. Then there are blockades, monster hunts, skeleton/zombie island take overs, contests, avatar outfitting, homes and ships of all sorts of sizes and designs to buy, paint, and decorate, parties to throw... Yeah. Lots to do.
As a game that was hugely social in its prime, seeing the excruciatingly slow and painful death of Y!PP (esp the sub oceans) was... really, really sad. I miss this game a LOT, and really wish it could be revived. Once Spiral Knights started to take off, things went downhill.
I've never really found any other games quite like PP. The thorough permeation of theme, the way it was kid-friendly but not so much so that it was off-putting or unappealing to adults, how one could play casually, socially, or fer-srs. This game is both niche yet massively appealing to the masses, especially in the casual mobile gaming world of today.
What would be SUPER. FREAKING. AWESOME! ? If Y!PP were to produce a sequel, or a spiritual successor, or something like that. The system itself worked quite well - $10/month subscription is very fair. Some things would need to be reworked a bit, and I can EASILY see how expansive it could get. An enormous open-world you could explore on your own or with your crew, finding hidden, previously undiscovered islands in the far corners of the world, exploring overwhelming jungles, diving into the deep-sea ruins of Atlantis in search of treasure and adventure, brave the misty swamplands of the cursed isles, all while interacting with diverse wildlife and a population of both advanced AI NPCs and other players; yet  still keeping the original base concept of the game (crews, pillages, plunders, and puzzles)...  I lost many hundreds of hours to the original Y!PP - and I can easily see myself pouring hundreds more into its successor, if it were done right.
But right now? The game isn't worth playing unless you want a poor social experience (if any), a few puzzles to play (these days the only puzzles you can play without a subscription are ship duty puzzles such as bilge, carp, sails, rigs, etc), and an empty, empty, linear world in which you don't so much explore as you do sail in a straight light along a pre-dotted path from island to island, archipelago to archipelago. Perhaps you could even buy up a stash of little blue potions and whisk yourself to quiet, abandoned port towns and long-forgotten jungle islands, just to see what could have been.

屋上の百合霊さん, officially translated to Kindred Spirits on the Roof, is a Visual Novel about love. Girls love, to be more precise. The protagonist of our story is Toomi Yuna, a student of Kokonotsuboshi Girls Academy of Commerce. The plot sets in motion when she encounters the ghost of two since long deceased girls who happened to fall in love with each other in the afterlife. These girls wish is to experience their ”first time” together, only problem is, they're just not sure exactly how to do it. Which is why they request for our protagonist to create a ”Yuritopia” at the school, by helping girls struggling with their feelings. For those not so versed in weeb vocab: They're basically asking her to make the school into a lesbian paradise.
And that's more or less it. I realize it sounds kinda dumb when I put it like that, but stick with me! What I described in the above paragraph might sound like some generic setup for some kind of porno or whatever, but be aware, this VN is far, far from what some people might want you to think. This is sadly the curse called prejudices this game is inherently burdened with. With the western VN market being such that it is, it's inevitable that it would at a glance be grouped with the likes of Nekopara or Sakura Beach etc. But I repeat, this is not the case. Kindred Spirits is not aimed at your usual western VN or Eroge demographic. If anything, Kindred Spirit panders more to the female readers than the male ones, as I feel it is completely devoid of the male gaze. Yes, there are sex-scenes. But then again, their focus and implementation relies more on the romantic aspects, rather the sexual ones. They are there not so you can get your rocks off, but to finalize and deepen the relationship you helped come to bloom. It's more beautiful than sexy, and cute rather than seductive. This is something that I feel needs to be brought to light, if just to ever so slightly elevate some of the prejudice plaguing this VN (or genre as a whole). It could certainly be seen as fanservicey or whatever the kids call it these days, but then again there is nothing inherently bad about that. Bottom line is that this VN is not offensive. It takes a concept that could easily make 100 times the profit by being a straight up Nukige, or self-insert Eroge, and instead makes something endearing and romantic out of it. That is at least commendable, if nothing else.
But enough of that. Is the story itself any good? Is there any gameplay? The story itself is nothing complicated at all (which you could probably tell from the synopsis alone), but nor does it try to be. It is simply a story about love. It just so happens to be between girls this time. It is both cute, charming and funny as hell at times. It is a straightforward love story, without much depth, twists or deeper meaning. If you're feeling up for some HNNNG's then this is the story for you.
The gameplay is not much to speak of to be honest, since the story is mostly linear. You won't have any bad endings or failed routes. Which also means that you won't alter the story overly much with your inputs, but rather reading a story. There's no fail state, game over, or dead ends, only love～. There are a couple of extra scenes and dialogue, but that's about it. The game time is somewhere between 10-30 hours. It is in other words, a relatively short to medium long-ish length VN depending on your reading speed. What I have seen of the translation so far is that it is not only up to par, but actually very good and genuine. It goes without saying that this is as good as it gets as an English reader.
TL;DR: If you are looking for a romance heavy Visual Novel without having to self-insert as a faceless protagonist to sex up some underage girls, this is probably as good as it gets. If you don't mind, or even prefer GL over vanilla,  then this is no doubt as good as it gets no matter your other preferences. If you're looking for porn/fanservice, or something to get your rocks off, you should probably look elsewhere. The same goes for those wanting a dark, mature or deep story of any kind. What you're paying for is a cute, well-written and funny love story that I urge you not to miss.
Anyways, those are my poorly written, hastily put together thoughts on this particular VN. Check it out I'd say. It's good. Ignore the usual prejudices, but at the same time, know what it is you're paying for when you buy it. I might come back to edit the review if it would prove necessary, but I'll get to that when I get to that.
Thanks for reading, and remember:「ユリトピア」にするために！

Story: The story set in Hong Kong you are Wei Shen an undercover police officer. You first start as acting as a drug smuggler who is soon arrested so you could meet up with an old friend called Jackie jail. This is the first step of the undercover mission your boss Thomas Pendrew has asked you to do as he wants the red poles down in Hong Kong. You will also deal with your Handler Raymond Mak and many others. I will leave it at that as I do not wish to give away too much.
Gameplay: Set in an open world. You control Wei Shen a Chinese American police officer as he goes undercover. Sleeping Dogs is played in a third person perspective action adventure game with roleplaying elements. You have the ability to walk, run, jump, climb over obstacles and swim. As well as use weapons and martial arts in combat. You can drive a variety of vehicles including cars, boats, and motorcycles.
The combat system revolves around hand to hand fighting. The cover system allows the player to move between cover, fire blindly, aim freely, and target a specific enemy. Individual body parts can also be targeted. While driving, Wei can get out and jump onto other moving vehicles. This is rather fun to do if you time it right.
Sleeping Dogs features role playing elements with three different experience point values Triad XP, Face XP, and Police XP. Triad XP and Police XP measure Wei's devotion to the triad and police, respectively, while Face XP is a measure of his general reputation. Clothing, accessories and vehicles are available for purchase by Wei, and have an effect on non player characters reactions. Sleeping Dogs tracks acquired skills in areas such as hand to hand combat, which improve through use in the game.
Now driving AI could be better along with speed control while you drive its not quite there but certainly did not stop me playing.
Controls: Controls are easy to use. You can use a game pad or just use the keyboard and mouse. Or switch between both like me. Game pad for driving, Fighting, walking around and keyboard and mouse for shooting.
The Graphics: The graphics do look really good. Some things like the blood at first had me going a bit iffy at it but once deeper into the game I never noticed it. They certainly have done a good job in my books.
Music: The music suits the area of course now the car music shame there was nothing more towards the GTA style's but they still worked. Even when I noticed the Kerrang station I never left that channel.
Bugs and Glitches: Truthfully I never seen any myself that would cause any issues to ruin the gameplay enjoyment.
Replay Value: There is certainly replay value there as there is many dlc data there which includes Nightmare in North Point, Year of the Snake and The Zodiac Tournament (this on can be played in the main story). But I will certainly be playing it again for the dlc and even the main story line to.
Overall: I have to say Sleeping dog's is another good game that is out there in the waters with the likes of GTA and Saints Row. As you can see I certainly enjoyed it and have been impressed. With the replay value it certainly is worth having. So I give this game 9 paws out of 10 as there is some improvement for it to do to hit top mark in my book.

I absolutely love this game. I can really tell playing it that the developers had fun making the game and clearly enjoy their jobs. The Hong Kong portrayed in the game is vibrant, diverse, and chock full of detail, wherever you look. I love the assortment of vehicles, and how each one feels a little different. Being a car guy in real life, I love being able to assemble a "dream garage" of every car in the game by purchasing from the different vendors around the city.
The hand-to-hand combat is solid, not quite as solid as say Arkham Asylum, but certainly satisfying enough. The gunplay is decent, the only thing that lets this part of the game down is absolutely any lack of an inventory system, so any guns you use must be found in the environment. Which is frustrating, given that the DLC packs add some pretty interesting weapons (the Deus Ex rifle, for one), but you rarely get to use them in missions.
Overall, this is an excellent free-roaming adventure game that has a fair amount of replay value, and is strengthened by the fact the game doesn't take itself too seriously. Between the cars, combat, and the assortment of colorful characters, this is a game that has earned itself a place near and dear to my heart. Well done.

Half life tells an interesting story...
But it tells it very poorly.
Essentially the idea of the game is that you are a scientist in Black Mesa, and because you suck at your job you bring aliens into your world. Not a bad idea, in fact half life 2 is a pretty good game that follows the same story much later.
However, the problems and glitches in this game make it TERRIBLE to play.
1. In the opening sequence a headcrab got out of its tank where it was supposed to stay and murdered the scientist who was supposed to open a door, making it impossible to continue.
2. You can literally skip several weapons by accident.
3. The sound effects are bad, and you hear them all like 40 times a second.
4. Health packs are placed in the worst locations, often requiring you to kill everyone in the room before using one which, when you are at low health most of the time, becomes a serious problem.
5. There are tons of cheap deaths in this game. That pipe you were travelling through? It literally falls, killing you. That bridge you're walking across does it, too. The game doesn't teach you about the stupid cieling monsters, so unless you knew they existed beforehand, you are going to die.
6. You have to do everything through trial and error.
7. The audio is just bad. People talk over eachother. You can't hear anything they're saying. Not that it matters, though. I don't care about the story because playing this game is a nightmare.
8. All of the scientists look the same, so I don't care about any of them. I got bored and, every time one tried to say something, I outright murdered them
9. The game doesn't teach you anything. You have to learn everything on your own. The controls, how things work, what you can break and what you can't. No clever game design teaches you any of it.
10. The graphics are very lacking. I know it's an old game, but jesus can't you make outside look more like outside and less like... I dunno, a pile of crap? (There is no grass I guarentee it to you.)
Half life 2 fixes almost (if not all of) these problems.

Simple-looking but broad and addictive game. If you long for the feel of oldschool Runescape, a nice community, and a low commitment level that lets you fit some gaming into your busy schedule, give RPG MO a try. The breadth of gathering and crafting skills has kept me busy for many hours already, and I've only scratched the surface of the possibilities with combat, world exporation, and group content.
+ Wide breadth of skills to pursue, with some unusual ones like farming, breeding, and jewelry.
+ Combat system is simple enough that you can start fighting monsters without much thought, but has depth if you feel like optimizing how you balance and level-up your combat skills or trying your hand at magic or archery.
+ The market system provides a wonderfully convenient and low-friction way of buying and selling items to other players.
+ Choose a low-attention activity like mining or fishing to multitask while still making progress in the game (I like to write code and watch shows). Or frankly any activity, since combat is passive and monsters don't chase you.
+ Runs well on laggy/unstable internet connections.
+ Great community with helpful and entertaining in-game chat.
- There's not much of an adrenaline rush to be had; this game is pretty slow-paced.
- High skill levels require a
grind.
- The global double experience events (purchased by players, pretty cool!) tend to happen on weekends and/or on European time zones, which might mean you miss out on most of them.
